item.title: 2027: City Boy Movement targets 500,000 Enugu students for Tinubu
item.description: By Chinedu Adonu The City Boy Movement has launched a membership registration drive across tertiary institutions in Enugu State, targeting 500,000 students as part of its mobilisation efforts for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027. The South-East Zonal Coordinator of the movement’s Membership Registration and Data Management, Dr. Onyeka Nwafor, disclosed this during a membership registration exercise in Enugu. Nwafor said the movement had partnered with the Council of Students’ Union Government Presidents in Enugu State (COSPEN) to expand its membership base and mobilise students across campuses in support of Tinubu’s second-term ambition. He said the initiative was aimed at strengthening the movement’s presence in the South-East and demonstrating student support for the President’s administration. Also speaking, the COSPEN Chairman and President of the Students’ Union Government of the Institute of Management and Technology (IMT), Enugu, Comrade Emmanuel Nwankwo, said student leaders had endorsed Tinubu’s re-election bid, citing the impact of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND). Nwankwo pledged that the council would mobilise more than 500,000 students for the registration exercise. He spoke during a meeting with Nwafor at Tiger Bar, Enugu, where both parties discussed strategies for expanding membership registration and improving coordination across campuses. “Many of our peers would have dropped out of school because of financial constraints, but NELFUND has eased the burden on parents and helped students remain in school. For this, we believe Mr President deserves a second term,” he said. Describing COSPEN as the gatekeepers of tertiary institutions in the state, Nwankwo said the student loan scheme had helped address some of the financial difficulties confronting students. Nwafor, a former governorship aspirant of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Anambra State, said the movement was determined to expand its presence across tertiary institutions in the South-East. “We have resolved to scale up registration across campuses in Enugu. The registration exercise will demonstrate the level of student support for President Tinubu’s administration, particularly the impact of the student loan initiative,” he said. He added that COSPEN would coordinate the mobilisation exercise through student union presidents across the various institutions. item.title: ‘You should've stayed': Anderson QB Cove Darbyshire still healing from father's suicide
item.description: Anderson Trojans quarterback Cove Darbyshire (7) celebrates beating the Friendswood Mustangs 34-35 in a Class 5A Division I Bi-District Round playoff game at House Park, Nov. 15, 2025. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) C overt "Cove" Darbyshire always pictured his mom and dad walking the field with him on Senior night. Instead, the Anderson quarterback told the American-Statesman last week he felt a surge of emotions as he and his mother, Marion, took the stroll alone on the last Friday of October. A touch of understanding. Some sadness, and definitely anger. He turned to his mom. "He's not here," Marion recalled her son saying. "That f-r." Chad Darbyshire was found dead by suicide Sept. 5, 2021, two days after Cove's 13th birthday. He was 49 years old. His death rocked Cove, his mom, his older brother Blaise and his older sister Zuzu, who are processing their emotions to this day. But none of them were shocked. The Darbyshires knew Chad wasn't well. Marion learned he suffered from depression a year into their marriage. Despite her best efforts, he never quite opened up to her, or anyone, about the depth of his pain and where it stemmed from. Chad, a former creative director, artist and sketch writer, lit up rooms with his charisma, she said. He was the kind of person others loved to be around. To his family, he could be volatile, brilliant, complicated. Cove Darbyshire in his room at home in Austin, Nov. 10, 2026. Behind him, two of his father's drawings are displayed on the wall. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) The Darbyshires' story is imperfect. But as Cove enters the playoffs, he still wishes his father was in the stands, no matter how much he resents him for leaving. "It's ugly. It's hard. And no one should ever have to go through it," Marion said. "Because no matter how bad they might have been, you always wish they were here." 'Just play football' Cove Darbyshire said he didn't know he wanted to get serious about football until the seventh grade - the year his father died. He played a variety of sports until then, with soccer being the main alternative. Cove has had an athletic build from birth (Marion said he was born with a six-pack) but the family didn't know what he actually wanted to do with it. Then, the day after their dad's memorial, Blaise Darbyshire remembers Cove walking into his room around 10 p.m. He asked Blaise to wake him up at 5:30 a.m. so that he could go work out at Dell Jewish Community Center in Northwest Hills. The routine continued throughout Cove's entire seventh grade and half his eighth-grade year. He'd told his older siblings he wanted to make it to the NFL. Blaise, who took a year off college to grieve, was more than willing to help. "You've told me your goal," Blaise recounted to the Statesman in October. "I'm going to make sure you're keeping yourself accountable." Marion said Cove would train incessantly outside of school every day, including weekends. He'd schedule coaching appointments on h

item.title: Man Utd sack manager Carrick, with Pochettino set for hot seat
item.description: Michael Carrick has paid the price for Manchester United's disastrous start to the season (Oli SCARFF) Manchester United sacked manager Michael Carrick on Thursday after their worst-ever start to a Premier League campaign, with USA boss Mauricio Pochettino widely tipped to replace him. Former United captain Carrick led the team to an impressive third-place finish last season, but they have taken just eight points from 10 games in the current campaign and are in the relegation zone. The club confirmed in a statement that it had parted ways with the 45-year-old, following mounting speculation he would be axed during the international break. "After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions," United's statement said. "Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club." United said they intended to appoint a permanent successor "as quickly as possible". - Chaos - Carrick impressed after taking over as interim boss following Ruben Amorim's acrimonious exit in January, leading United to Champions League qualification. He was rewarded with a two-year permanent deal but, hampered by the club's underwhelming recruitment in the summer transfer window, his side have endured a steep decline this season. Carrick has struggled to maintain discipline, dropping captain Bruno Fernandes after he criticised his manager's tactics following a 4-1 thrashing at Champions League debutants Como. And defender Lisandro Martinez spoke out against the club's hierarchy over their lack of top-quality signings. Carrick's final game in charge was a chaotic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday, after which he stressed he would not walk away. United, however, have decided to act in the hope of saving their season after a paltry three wins from 15 games in all competitions. It is believed Carrick's future was decided on Wednesday during a meeting in Monaco involving co-owner Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox. Ex-Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann, most recently in charge of Germany, were in the early running but Pochettino has now emerged as the overwhelming favourite to be announced as Carrick's successor. The Argentine has extensive experience of the Premier League following spells in charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, and he also coached Paris Saint-Germain. Pochettino signed a contract extension to remain with the USA through to the 2030 World Cup just three months ago. But Sky Sports reported Wednesday that United have "reached a verbal agreement in principle" with Pochettino, who has been linked with a move to Old Trafford on several previous occasions, to become their new boss. item.title: 47 Years Later, the Best 'Peanuts' Quote About Life and Death Still Hits Just as Hard
item.description: You can track the evolution of the American comic strip through its typical depiction of childhood. Early 20th century strips like Ernie Bushmiller's Nancy (1933) show kids' lives as relatively prosaic, particularly given the culture and publication standards of the time. While their child protagonists might have faced some incidental frustrations, the comics page was mostly about gentle humor. Yes, Sluggo is a homeless orphan, but no, that isn't a source of angst or conflict.

item.title: Chinese woman accused of spying on Nvidia chief entered Taiwan 8 times
item.description: The woman accused of spying for Beijing during an affair with Nvidia founder Jensen Huang visited Taiwan a total of eight times in 2024 and 2025, a Taiwanese government minister said Thursday. Taiwan, a dominant player in the global semiconductor industry, sits at the centre of strategic competition between the United States and China, which claims the self-ruled island as part of its territory. Jensen Huang, chief executive of the US-based chip giant Nvidia, has admitted to having an extramarital affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who US officials believe was working for Chinese intelligence. Beijing has rejected the spying allegations. Alice Huang, who is also known as Huang Le, used a Hong Kong passport to enter Taiwan “under a standard business visitor status” and there were “no special flags” about her at the time, Mainland Affairs Council (MAC) Minister Chiu Chui-cheng told lawmakers. Chiu made the remarks in Taiwan’s parliament in response to lawmakers’ questions about Alice Huang’s entries into Taiwan and a New York Times report that the United States had advised Taiwan as early as 2024 to monitor her movements. “At least we at the Mainland Affairs Council did not receive any relevant information,” Chiu said. “If we had, we definitely would have stepped up our entry screening and border flow management.” Chiu said records show that Alice Huang visited Taiwan three times in 2024 and five times in 2025. The records do not show any entries for this year, he said. “If we had any of the kind of critical intelligence you mentioned, leading us to believe she posed a threat to Taiwanese society, we would have definitely flagged her for heightened review,” Chiu said. “For any case where there are doubts, we intensify the level of scrutiny, and if we determine there are security concerns, there is no way we would allow her to enter the country.” The government has said Taiwan’s security agencies are investigating the incident. Cabinet spokeswoman Michelle Lee said Thursday “there is currently no public information” about whether Alice Huang “is suspected of any criminal offence or on the related investigative procedures”. “If a criminal offence is involved, due to the principle of prosecutorial confidentiality during an ongoing investigation, we cannot provide any further comment,” Lee said. Alice Huang was seen at a dinner in May 2025 hosted by Jensen Huang at a Chinese restaurant in Taipei during Computex, the island’s top tech expo. Journalists stood outside the restaurant filming through glass windows and doors as Jensen Huang and a woman identified as Alice Huang, who was wearing a pink dress, mingled with other attendees. At one point, Jensen Huang can be seen putting his arm around Alice Huang as she kisses him on the right cheek, press livestreams show. The post Chinese woman accused of spying on Nvidia chief entered Taiwan 8 times appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Will Joseph and Max Ojomoh given chance to shine in radical England revamp for Japan
item.description: Will Joseph and Max Ojomoh have been given opportunities to impress in a much-changed starting side for an injury-hit England against Japan . Joseph will start on the wing and earn his first cap since the 2022 tour of Australia, while Ojomoh returns at inside centre for the first time since a player-of-the-match performance against Argentina last November. Henry Pollock earns just a second international start at No 8 after an eye-catching outing on the wing from the bench in the 45-22 success against Australia. George Ford starts ahead of Fin Smith at fly half, with Freddie Steward at full-back, Cadan Murley on the left wing and Jack van Poortvliet and Henry Slade the only backline starters retained from the Wallabies win. George Ford starts at fly half for England (Getty) Among the replacements, scrum half Archie McParland is in line for a debut, while Emmanuel Iyogun, Arthur Clark and Greg Fisilau will win their second caps. Steve Borthwick ’s squad had been hit by injuries to Ollie Chessum (shoulder), Seb Atkinson (hip), George Furbank (groin) and Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, with the hope that the former trio can feature against New Zealand next week. Feyi-Waboso has been ruled out of the remainder of the Nations Championship with an ankle issue. “Japan are a very well-coached side who will challenge us in different ways, and we know we’ll need to bring intensity throughout the game,” Borthwick said. “We’re all delighted for Archie. He’s had some bad luck with injury, so it’s especially pleasing to be able to name him in an England matchday 23 for the first time. He’s an outstanding young talent who has worked hard to get to this point, and we’re really looking forward to being back on Saturday.” Northampton’s Archie McParland will make his England debut (PA Wire) Fin Smith is understood to have trained fully this week but drops out of the matchday 23 entirely, perhaps with one eye on New Zealand next weekend. Marcus Smith again provides fly half cover as one of two backs on the bench. Alex Coles moves to the blindside with Chessum absent having scrummaged on the flank against Australia, and Asher Opoku-Fordjour is given a rare outing on the tighthead. In all, just five starters retain their spots, with Coles and Ben Earl among them but having moved positions. Japan, meanwhile, stick with a settled selection with Eddie Jones naming an unchanged forward pack from the defeat to Wales. Former England boss Eddie Jones takes his Japan side to Twickenham on Saturday (PA Wire) Riku Tokito is brought in on the wing for the injured Inoke Burua and will make his debut. The former Japan sevens international is yet to play a professional 15-a-side game, though Jones is confident he can handle an anticipated aerial bombardment from England. “It’s a big week for Japanese rugby,” Jones said. “England is the nation we’ve never been able to beat. Everyone knows the record. We want to do something different this week, and we’ve trained like that." England XV: 1 Ellis

item.title: Review: Apple's M6 iMac is pricey, but it's still a good choice for a clean desk
item.description: The Apple Silicon iMac got its fourth refresh this month. Every other Apple Silicon Mac has found a way to move forward over the last half-decade—we've gotten a more Pro design for the MacBook Pro, a mini-er design for the Mac mini, and a Mac Studio that has finally made Apple admit it doesn't want to make the Mac Pro anymore. But the Apple Silicon iMac has always been more interested in looking backward. It's the thin, screen-on-a-stand iMac design by way of the original Bondi Blue G3 iMac. It's a clean and pretty desktop computer, one I see all the time in small offices and on TV shows that depict small offices. We're long past the days when it was Apple's primary workstation computer. item.title: 2027: I was told to spend N500m before contesting — Accord Party candidate, Olajengbesi
item.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — The Accord Party candidate for Oriade/Obokun Federal Constituency, Pelumi Olajengbesi, has alleged that he was told to be prepared to throw away N500 million before he could be taken seriously as a political contender in Ijesa North. Olajengbesi made the allegation in an open letter addressed to elders and stakeholders of Ijesa North, both at home and abroad, in which he urged the people to resist what he described as an attempt to extend the tenure of the incumbent lawmaker, Wole Oke, to 28 years. A copy of the letter was made available to Vanguard in Abuja on Thursday. Recounting his first attempt to join the political race, Olajengbesi said he expressed interest in contesting for the House of Representatives in August 2016, when he was 30 years old and had limited financial resources. He alleged that Hon. Niyi Ajifowobaje, whom he described as one of Oke’s prominent political associates at the time, told him that an aspirant in Ijesa North must be prepared to throw N500 million into a river before considering a contest for the Oriade/Obokun seat. According to him, Ajifowobaje further suggested that an aspirant would need as much as N1 billion to be taken seriously. “I was told to throw away N500 million before running in Ijesa North,” he said. Olajengbesi said he subsequently assembled a group of young people in the constituency on July 11, 2017, to examine the incumbent’s political strengths and identify alternative approaches to representation. He said the group produced a 16-page report, which he had incorporated into a book he was writing. According to him, the report concluded that money was the major political advantage the incumbent brought to the table, rather than ideas, innovation or inspiration for younger generations. “Money was the only thing he was bringing to the table. No ideas, no innovation, no inspiration, no storytelling, nothing to inspire younger people. Just money without excellence,” he quoted the report as saying. He said the report also observed that several professionals and educated people in the constituency were dissatisfied with the quality of representation but were reluctant to support a challenger unless they were convinced the person had sufficient financial resources to sustain the contest. Olajengbesi alleged that the incumbent had cultivated an image of political dominance that made some potential challengers believe they could not compete with his financial strength. He further alleged that Oke once boasted during a private conversation about his election spending and how he had dealt with previous challengers. According to Olajengbesi, Oke allegedly claimed to have paid for the return journeys of some aspirants based abroad and financially settled local contenders. He declined to identify the individuals allegedly mentioned in the conversation. item.title: Led by 4-star QB, Bastrop eyeing deep postseason run, hoping to build off last year
item.description: Pflugerville receiver Trace Lamar (7) fumbles the ball on a dive into the endzone during the game against Bastrop at Bastrop Memorial Stadium on Friday, Oct. 16, 2026 in Cedar Creek, Texas. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) BASTROP - Midway through the regular season, it may have been easier to name the Bastrop football players off the field rather than the ones competing on Friday nights. A Bears squad that entered the season with high expectations after making the third round of the playoffs last year dropped four of their first five games as a rash of injuries sidelined around a dozen starters. But Bastrop healed up right before district play and cruised to the District 12-5A Division II title. Now, the largely healthy Bears (6-4, 5-0) open postseason play Friday against Victoria West on a five-game winning streak and hope to go even further in the Class 5A, Division II bracket than they did a year ago. MORE: Best shots for a state title? Westlake and this other Austin-area school "This year, for whatever reason, we've caught the bad side of (injuries)," Bastrop coach Jake Griedl told the American-Statesman earlier this week. "But even in those tough moments, there have been plenty of players step up and do things right; intentionally correct, with great discipline and high effort, and that's what ultimately makes really good teams really successful are those factors. Now that we are healthy and we feel like we got our kids playing with those three factors, we're excited to see what happens in the playoffs." Bastrop captains take the field for the coin toss ahead of the game against Pflugerville at Bastrop Memorial Stadium on Friday, Oct. 16, 2026 in Cedar Creek, Texas. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Injuries lead to a difficult start One of the most important moments of Bastrop's season happened on Sept. 25 at the end of the fourth quarter of a defeat to Brenham. Quarterback Brennon Hopkins, who was in due to an injury to starter Weston Nielsen, fumbled as he got hit on the final play of the 40-3 loss. The ball was scooped up by a Brenham defender, who had nothing but grass in front of him. Instead of letting the defender run to the goal line untouched for a meaningless score, Hopkins, as well as running back Jahmani Jones-Watkins, chased down the Cubs defender and tackled him less than five yards from the end zone. "That for us was a teaching point of even when you're going through it, the effort that it takes to be great still needs to be seen," Griedl said. Through its first five games, Bastrop was forced to trust unproven players all over the field. Nielsen, the team's four-star quarterback committed to Arizona State, got injured in the season opener. He headlined a list of standouts unavailable for the Bears that included a starting linebacker, arguably the team's top receiver, a starting safety and a right guard. item.title: Tom Brady vs. Will Smith: Which Celebrity’s Team Will Win the E1 Championship?
item.description: The electric-boat league will crown a new winner this weekend. The Bombay Sapphire E1 Miami Grand Prix, taking place on Biscayne Bay on November 13 and 14, will determine this season’s champions . Teams backed by A-listers including Tom Brady, Rafael Nadal, Will Smith, Marc Anthony, LeBron James, and Steve Aoki will compete in two races on consecutive days, marking the championship’s first double-header. More from Robb Report Mercedes-Benz's New Holographic Tech Will Turn Your Windshield Into a Screen Chris Hemsworth's New Gin Was Made Using Honey From His Australian Farm This $14 Million Equestrian Estate Sits Within a Double-Gated Orange County Community “This is set to be an incredible finale to the 2026 Championship and a landmark weekend for E1 as we stage our first double-header,” E1 C.E.O. Jamie Copas said in a statement. “ With two races on consecutive days, there is still much to play for as teams look to finish the season on a high.” Team Brady, which won the opening two E1 world titles in 2024 and 2025, respectively, looks particularly strong heading into the championship showdown. Pilots Emma Kimiläinen and Sam Coleman have been on the podium at every round this year, securing 157 points for the team. The E1 Jeddah GP in January. Photo by Malcolm Griffiths/Getty Images That’s not to say Team Brady has it in the bag. Will Smith’s Westbrook Racing is trailing 40 points behind, but could still clinch the championship. Pilots Sara Price and Lucas Ordóñez, who have notched 82 points throughout the season, will have to need to return to the winning form they had earlier in the races and sweep the weekend to become victors. As for who comes next, Steve Aoki’s Aoki Racing Team sit third with 86 points, while LeBron’s Team AlUla are just two points further back. A podium finish would be especially meaningful for Aoki, given the DJ was born in Miami. “Amazing to see my team tearing it up in my home race again,” adds Aoki. “We fought all season to get our way into the Championship top three, and there’s no better place to finish the season strong than in front of a Miami crowd.” Those in Miami can watch the E1 RaceBirds “fly” across the water from the E1 Ocean Club. Title partner Bombay Sapphire is also holding an exclusive race-day celebration on a private Team Brady yacht docked at the Ocean Club. (Passes for E1 Ocean Club are available through Fever .) Fans at home across the U.S. can watch all the racing action on CBS Sports. (For those abroad, check out how to watch here .) item.title: Siena basketball's win at Dayton brings back great memories for Fenlon
item.description: Siena senior Conner Fenlon scores at the end of the second half of their 86-75 victory over Canisius at the Times Union Center on Sunday Feb. 26, 2012 in Albany, N.Y. He finished with a career high five points. (Philip Kamrass / Times Union ) (Philip Kamrass) After reenacting one of the great moments in Siena men's basketball history, Saints radio analyst and former player Conner Fenlon watched from the press table as the program added to its memorable history at University of Dayton Arena. He and play-by-play partner Emmanuel Berbari called Siena's 99-89 victory over the Flyers of the Atlantic 10 on Tuesday night before a sellout crowd of 13,407. It was a signature road win for the Saints in Nevada Smith's third game as head coach. "You're going on the road, early in the season, A10-level team," Fenlon said Wednesday. "The one thing about Dayton, they love their basketball there. They've sold out every year for I don't know how long (97 straight home games). They've got a good team. For Siena to go in there and play as well as they did, almost 100 points put on a team like that on the road, says a lot about Coach Smith and what these guys are believing in what he's preaching." It was Fenlon's first time in UD Arena since he was a Siena freshman walk-on guard in 2008-09. The ninth-seeded Saints knocked off No. 8 Ohio State 74-72 in double overtime in an NCAA Tournament first-round game. The victory is best remembered for point guard Ronald Moore's two 3-pointers. The first tied the game with 3.5 seconds left in the first overtime. The second won the game with 3.9 seconds left in the second overtime. Fenlon celebrated with his teammates on the Siena bench. "I haven't been there in a long time and it brought back a lot of memories," said Fenlon, 36, who is a controller at Albany Steel in Menands. "I always say, I don't think I'm in the position I am now if it wasn't for those teams and the success we had. It was so much fun to be back there." Siena also defeated Alcorn State in an NCAA opening-round game in Dayton in 2002, six years before Fenlon's arrival. After the team's morning shootaround on Tuesday, Siena assistant athletic director for communications Mike Demos wanted to recreate Moore's game-winner. With Berbari filming, Demos imitated former Siena guard Edwin Ubiles, who up-faked and passed the ball to Moore on the right wing for the winning shot. Except this time it was Fenlon, who still coaches AAU basketball but hadn't shot the ball in a big arena in a long time. "It was just for some fun and a laugh," said Fenlon, who posted the video on his X account @_cjf20. "The whole team was watching because they were putting their shoes on. Had a little pressure. I missed the first two, but ended up hitting the third." Once the real game started, Siena junior point guard Pace Prosser put on a performance against Dayton that would have made Moore proud. item.title: Donte Whitner names team that will stop the Minnesota Vikings from getting to the Super Bowl after Kirk Cousins trade
item.description: Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings have been solid defensively this season but their quarterback position had been a problem up until the Kirk Cousins trade. Carson Wentz once again struggled in the Vikings’ last game against the Buffalo Bills. He has one of the lowest completion rates (48.4%) in the NFL this season, which was causing problems for Minnesota on the offence. By contrast, Cousins has managed a 64.1% completion rate for the Las Vegas Raiders to this point and has 2,340 passing yards. But despite Cousins looking like a big upgrade for the Vikings, Donte Whitner still thinks they will struggle to get to the Super Bowl. Speaking via the NFL Network, Whitner suggested the arrival of Cousins could help them ‘all the way to the NFC Championship’ but the San Francisco 49ers could be the team that stops them reaching the Super Bowl. He said: “Minnesota’s defence, they have been carrying this team on their backs. “Kirk Cousins just showed up to help move the furniture. And if all goes well, like Kyle said, he could be moving that furniture all the way to the NFC Championship. “I’m not going to say Super Bowl yet because I still think they’re going to have to overcome the San Francisco 49ers.” Still, it will be interesting to see how the Vikings now look with a new quarterback when they clash with the Green Bay Packers this weekend. As for the 49ers, they, on paper, have a fairly easy game against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 10. item.title: Pep Guardiola to USMNT? Legendary manager emerges as SHOCK candidate to replace Mauricio Pochettino as Man Utd move nears
item.description: Manchester City v Chelsea FC - Premier League - Getty Images Sport Pep Guardiola has emerged as a spectacular candidate to take over the United States men's national team if Mauricio Pochettino leaves for Manchester United. The former Manchester City manager is currently a free agent and has previously expressed a deep admiration for the long-term sporting potential of the country. Shock candidate for USMNT United have officially dismissed Carrick , creating a major managerial domino effect. USMNT boss Pochettino has emerged as the overwhelming favourite to take the reins at Old Trafford . This sudden development has forced US Soccer to search for potential successors. According to The Athletic , Guardiola has been discussed at multiple levels within the USMNT hierarchy as a top candidate. The 55-year-old is currently without a club after his ten-year spell at Manchester City ended this summer . An ambitious American dream Appointing Guardiola would represent a monumental coup for American football, but the move remains highly speculative. The Spanish tactician has never managed at the international level and is accustomed to working with global superstars like Lionel Messi and Erling Haaland. However, Guardiola has previously expressed genuine admiration for the country. Speaking in 2024, he revealed his intrigue regarding American football. "The USA is fascinating when it comes to building a long-term project and taking the national team to the next level," Guardiola stated. "The potential of the USA is there given the population, the different sports and all of that." Guardiola also has a personal connection to the United States. Following his departure from Barcelona in 2012, he spent a year-long sabbatical living in New York. Overcoming the European competition Guardiola has already rejected international offers since leaving City. Earlier this year, he turned down the chance to manage the Italy national team to prioritise a personal sabbatical. Italian football federation president Giovanni Malago confirmed the approach to La Repubblica . Malago explained: "Pep was honest. He took some time out, also for family reasons. But if he had done something, he would have done it with us." Awaiting the Old Trafford domino Any formal approach from US Soccer depends entirely on Pochettino finalising a move to United. Until the Premier League club appoint Carrick's official successor, the USMNT managerial situation remains in limbo. If Pochettino does depart after this international break, the international schedule could work in Guardiola's favour. The USMNT do not play their next competitive fixtures until March, meaning the Spaniard could continue his planned break for several more months before returning to the dugout. For now, the football world will watch closely to see if United secure Pochettino. If they do, US Soccer could launch one of the most audacious managerial pursuits in history.

Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Since the federal probe into Malik Beasley ‘s betting scandal began last year, many details have come to light . Although the guard vehemently denied these allegations initially, his latest decision to plead guilty has led him down an interesting path. With reports indicating that Malik Beasley owed money to several creditors, including his barber , the former NBA player is in clear need of funds. Since the opportunities are limited, given his ongoing lawsuit, Beasley has seemingly turned to selling his autographed, game-worn jerseys. For obvious reasons, it is sad to see the veteran sharpshooter in such a condition. However, NBA fans did not hold back while reacting to the video in the comments. Here are a few reactions from fans on X: “That lawsuit hit bro HARD!” shared one user. “Malik Beasley thinks people want his jerseys,” commented another. “That s–t not game-worn. He had another one right in his lap and a pen in his hand. He’s signing that s–t right there on Live lol. S–t not worth a penny,” observed one fan. “Gambled all the money away. Now he’s begging lol,” stated another user. “Malik Beasley must have spent all his NBA money,” added another. As one fan noted, given that Beasley had the jerseys on his lap and readily at his disposal, there is good reason to doubt the authenticity of them being game-worn. With this factor accounted for, the value of the commodity would also drop dramatically, an unfortunate outcome for the former NBA player. Although some fans took the moment to roast Beasley, it is quite a sad sight. Given that he earned nearly $59,948,525 to $60,019,256 over the course of his nine-year-long NBA career, seeing the 29-year-old in this state is quite shocking. At one time, Malik Beasley was perceived as one of the best shooters in the NBA, having finished second in three-pointers made (3PM) with a total of 319 for the 2024-25 season. Given that he also finished in the 6MOY race that season, the veteran guard was due for a big payday from the Detroit Pistons . Sadly for Beasley, the investigations into his betting scandal began in the summer of 2025 , leading the Pistons to hold off on offering a new contract. item.title: 2027: INEC must earn voters’ trust before election day — IPC
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The International Press Centre (IPC) has urged officials of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to build public confidence in the electoral body ahead of the 2027 general elections through transparent conduct, accurate information and effective communication. The Executive Director of IPC, Dr. Lanre Arogundade, said public trust in the commission must be established long before election day, warning that misinformation, disinformation and inaccurate communication could undermine the credibility of the electoral process. Arogundade spoke on Wednesday in Kano at a two-day capacity-building engagement for INEC’s Voter Education and Publicity (VEP) and gender officials on electoral trust, effective communication, legal literacy and voter engagement. He noted that INEC had become a major subject of public discussions surrounding the elections, including disagreements among political parties and their supporters, even when the commission was not directly involved in such disputes. He said the manner in which INEC officials respond to public concerns and clarify issues could either strengthen or weaken confidence in the electoral body. “Every public interaction can either deposit or withdraw institutional trust,” he said. Arogundade explained that the training was designed to deepen the officials’ understanding of the Electoral Act, improve their communication skills, prepare them for crisis situations and equip them with the ability to verify and respond to false information. He stressed that VEP officials must be able to explain electoral laws and procedures in simple language, particularly when disputes arise or tensions develop during the electoral process. He warned that inaccurate responses to questions about electoral laws and voting procedures could damage the commission’s credibility more than withholding an answer. “A vague or inaccurate answer from a VEP official, for example, on legal questions around the Electoral Act or voting procedures can cost the commission more than silence would,” he said. The IPC director also called on INEC to establish dedicated fact-checking units in its state offices to identify and respond promptly to false information circulating about the commission. He said the officials would be introduced to social media listening techniques to monitor conversations about INEC in their respective states and provide clarifications where necessary. Arogundade expressed concern over the growing use of artificial intelligence to generate misleading content, noting that voices could be cloned within minutes and election result sheets falsified within seconds. Also speaking, the Executive Director of the Centre for Media and Society (CEMESO), Dr. Akin Akingbulu, said building public trust required more than issuing public statements, urging INEC to match its promises with concrete actions. “Walk the talk. That is, do what they are supposed to do to deliver a credible election. Be honest with the

item.title: Mississippi State’s 41 points without Kamario Taylor explain his reported $7.5 million deal to return in 2027
item.description: Kamario Taylor is finalizing a deal to return to the Mississippi State Bulldogs in 2027 that will make him the highest-paid quarterback in college football, On3’s Chris Low and Pete Nakos reported Wednesday . The deal is worth $7.5 million and could climb past $9 million with incentives. Taylor has played less than a quarter of football since Oct. 3, and Mississippi State is paying him like a player who never left the field. With Taylor healthy, Mississippi State opened 4-0 and scored 172 points, an average of 43 per game, capped by a 31-24 win over the No. 19 Missouri Tigers on Sept. 26. He hurt his toe in that game, played through it in a 56-23 loss to the Alabama Crimson Tide, sat out at the LSU Tigers and left the Oklahoma Sooners game in the first quarter. The school announced on Oct. 27 that he would miss the rest of the season with a foot injury requiring surgery and said he is expected to return at 100 percent. Oct 24, 2026; Starkville, Mississippi, USA; Mississippi State Bulldogs quarterback Kamario Taylor (1) passes the ball during warm ups prior to the game against the Oklahoma Sooners at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images In the four games Taylor either missed or did not finish, Mississippi State scored 41 points total. The Bulldogs were shut out 31-0 at LSU, lost 23-15 to Oklahoma, managed three points in a 31-3 loss to the Texas Longhorns and dropped a 25-23 decision at home to the Vanderbilt Commodores last Saturday. A team that climbed to No. 16 in the AP poll at the end of September now sits at 4-5 on a five-game losing streak, and those 41 points are the clearest measure available of what Taylor is worth to it. Why Mississippi State moved on Kamario Taylor before the portal ESPN’s Pete Thamel posted Wednesday that the deal was expected to be completed later in the day and called it significant for head coach Jeff Lebby’s portal recruiting and roster building. He then passed along what a source told ESPN about the effect Taylor has on other players. “One of the thing we realized is the level of quality players who are intrigued by joining Kamario at Mississippi State,” the source said. Lebby heads into the transfer window with a five-game skid on the books, a 5-8 finish in 2025 and a team that needs two wins in its last three games just to reach .500. A signed quarterback is the one thing a portal target can see on a depth chart before he commits, and Taylor’s 4-0 start is the most recent picture of what this program looks like with a full-strength offense. Getting the number done in November puts that picture in front of recruits before anyone else can make Taylor an offer. Oct 24, 2026; Starkville, Mississippi, USA; Mississippi State Bulldogs quarterback Kamario Taylor (1) walks off the field after the game against the Oklahoma Sooners at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. item.title: Former Michigan interim HC Biff Poggi sends message about Wolverines that leaves out coaches
item.description: The Michigan Wolverines are 5-4 and 2-4 in the Big Ten after a 15-6 home loss to the Michigan State Spartans on Saturday, a game in which the Spartans kicked five field goals, forced four turnovers and recorded five sacks to beat Michigan for the first time since 2021. On Wednesday, the man who coached many of those players through last season’s bowl game went on X to speak up for them. “I know the kids on this Michigan team. It is not going as they hoped. However, they will not be broken, discouraged or quit. There is a lot of toughness and determination in that group. Selling them short is a mistake. So many complex issues go into a season. GoBlue. I believe,” Biff Poggi wrote. Michigan acting head coach Biff Poggi walks onto the field for second half against Central Michigan at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Sept. 13, 2025. I know the kids on this Michigan team. It is not going as they hoped. However, they will not be broken, discouraged or quit. There is a lot of toughness and determination in that group. Selling them short is a mistake. So many complex issues go into a season. GoBlue. I believe. — Biff poggi (@BiffPoggi) November 11, 2026 Poggi was Michigan’s associate head coach when Sherrone Moore was fired last December, ran the program as interim head coach through the bowl game and now works as a Big Ten Network studio analyst. He has said the search that followed came down to him and Kyle Whittingham, and that he believed he had the job. What Biff Poggi said about Michigan’s coaches in October This is the second time in three weeks Poggi has asked Michigan fans for patience, and the two posts are built differently. After the 13-6 overtime loss to the Indiana Hoosiers left Michigan at 4-3, he opened with a defense of everyone in the building. “To all of my Michigan friends. First, GoBLUE. Second, no one is getting fired. Please relax. The team is 4-3. It is a new staff, a very good staff,” Poggi wrote in late October, adding that the worst thing Michigan supporters could do was abandon the players and coaches when they struggled. To all of my Michigan friends. First ,GoBLUE. Second, no one is getting fired. Please relax. The team is 4-3. It is a new staff, a very good staff. The worst thing we can do as Michigan supporters is abandon the players and coaches when they struggle. It is exactly at this time that they need us most. Let’s see some support for all the coaches and players. — Biff poggi (@BiffPoggi) October 25, 2026 Wednesday’s post names the players, their toughness and their determination, and stops there. Whittingham, offensive coordinator Jason Beck and the rest of the staff go unmentioned, and the line about complex issues leaves open where those issues come from. Earlier this month, in the same week he discussed finishing second to Whittingham , Poggi said publicly that Michigan’s offense was not playing Michigan football. item.title: How to Style a Pink Buba With a Mini Skirt: Alex Unusual’s Loving Itohan Look
item.description: Alex Unusual’s gold grillz, crystal floral choker, and cherub-accented sunglasses. Who says a buba has to be paired with a wrapper? Nigerian actress, media personality, and reality television star Asogwa Alexandra A —popularly known as Alex Unusua l—is giving us another way to wear the traditional Yoruba top, and her look for the premiere of Loving Itohan makes a strong case for pairing it with a mini skirt. The actress chose a bright fuchsia satin buba with wide half-sleeves, styling it with a fitted mini skirt made from emerald-green and magenta floral brocade damask . It’s an interesting way to rethink the familiar iro and bubacombination: keep the traditional top, swap the wrapper for a shorter skirt, and let the difference in fabric and colour give the outfit its character. The smooth finish of the pink satin against the patterned damask also shows how to wear two statement fabrics without making them compete . The trick is to give each piece a clear role, with the pink buba providing a bold block of colour and the brocade bringing in pattern and texture. Alex Unusual puts a modern spin on the Yoruba iro and buba with a satin top and brocade mini skirt. The mini skirt also gives the outfit a contemporary take on the Oleku silhouette, which traditionally pairs a loose or fitted buba with a wrapper tied above the knee. Alex’s version plays with that familiar proportion, using a fitted damask skirt in place of the wrapper. If you are wondering how to wear a buba and mini skirt without the proportions feeling off, the secret is balancing volume with structure. Because a traditional buba comes with a relaxed cut and wide sleeves, tucking it cleanly into a fitted, high-waisted mini skirt defines the waist and keeps the silhouette neat rather than boxy. Mixing textures intentionally helps too—pairing a plain silk, satin, or AsoOke top with a patterned damask, jacquard, or beaded mini skirt lets both pieces complement each other rather than clash. Alex Unusual in her contemporary Yoruba buba and mini skirt outfit for the Loving Itohan premiere. She carried the damask into her gele, which was wrapped high into voluminous, sculptural folds. An oversized gold lip-shaped brooch secured one side, adding another detail to the headpiece. Using the same fabric for the skirt and gele also helped bring the different parts of the outfit together, while keeping the pink buba at the centre of the colour story. It’s a styling idea worth borrowing if you’re working with patterned damask and want your accessories to feel connected to the rest of your outfit. Alex Unusual pairs her damask gele with cherub-detailed sunglasses, layered gold jewellery, and custom grillz. Alex’s jewellery and accessories added even more detail. She layered a crystal floral choker with a long gold lariat necklace featuring a stirrup-style drop, then added chunky gold cuff bangles on both wrists and sculptural gold rings. item.title: Why Alabama’s real Vanderbilt concern may be closer to home than Kalen DeBoer suggests
item.description: Kalen DeBoer used his Wednesday night Hey Coach radio show to push back on the questions he has fielded all week about the Vanderbilt Commodores, the 4-5 team the No. 3 Alabama Crimson Tide visit on Saturday in Nashville, and he aimed his answer at the people asking them. “I can tell by the questions as I go through interviews throughout the course of the week that everyone outside of the building hasn’t watched Vanderbilt. They haven’t watched them. Our guys understand what it looks like. They’re preparing for it, and having a good week of practice right now,” DeBoer said , as relayed by Bama 24/7’s Mike Rodak. Oct 24, 2026; Tuscaloosa, AL, USA; Alabama head coach Kalen DeBoer leaves the field after Alabama’s win at Saban Field at Bryant Denny Stadium. Alabama defeated Texas A&M 31-20. Mandatory Credit: Gary Cosby Jr.-Tuscaloosa News The last time Alabama went to Nashville, it arrived ranked No. 1 after beating the Georgia Bulldogs and lost 40-35 on Oct. 5, 2024. DeBoer brought that game up with his players in the visitors’ locker room at Tiger Stadium on Saturday night, minutes after a 31-13 win over the LSU Tigers. Kalen DeBoer on Hey Coach: “I can tell by the questions as I go through interviews throughout the course of the week that everyone outside of the building hasn’t watched Vanderbilt. They haven’t watched them.” “Our guys understand what it looks like. They’re preparing for it, and having a good week of practice right now.” — Mike Rodak (@mikerodak) November 12, 2026 “A lot of these guys don’t have the memory from a couple years ago. Big win, then going up to Vanderbilt,” DeBoer told Crimson Tide Sports Network radio postgame. Does Vanderbilt’s tape back up Kalen DeBoer? Vanderbilt opened 3-0, lost five straight and then won 25-23 at the Mississippi State Bulldogs last Saturday, and part of that losing streak supports DeBoer. Two of those five losses were decided by 10 points or fewer, 21-15 at the Auburn Tigers and 31-21 at home against the Arkansas Razorbacks. At the Kentucky Wildcats, then ranked No. 12, the Commodores trailed only 24-17 going into the fourth quarter before losing 34-17. Georgia beat Vanderbilt 38-14 in Athens, and the Ole Miss Rebels put up 52 points in Nashville. Vanderbilt also ranks next-to-last in the SEC in rushing at 112.1 yards per game, and its 160 rushing yards at Mississippi State were its most against an FBS opponent all season. A team that hangs around into the second half against SEC opponents is a fair warning for a coach to issue, and DeBoer has the 2024 result to justify issuing it loudly. The stronger case for concern, though, sits inside his own building. LSU outgained Alabama 457-285 on Saturday and crossed midfield on each of its first seven drives, and Alabama won because its defense allowed 10 points on four red-zone trips. item.title: Philip Rivers reportedly accepts NC State head coaching job ahead of Friday board vote
item.description: The NC State Wolfpack board of trustees is expected to finalize a contract Friday that makes Philip Rivers the program’s next head football coach, ESPN’s Pete Thamel and Mark Schlabach reported Wednesday . The full board meets Friday morning in Raleigh, and the agenda ends with a closed session, according to WRAL News . Rivers, 44, is in his sixth season as head coach at St. Michael Catholic High School in Fairhope, Alabama, a program he started from nothing and took to the state semifinals in 2024 and 2025. He has never coached in college or the NFL. Per ESPN’s report, he told NC State he wanted to finish the high school season before anything moved forward, and that season ended last Friday with a 42-35 home playoff loss to The Glenwood School. Health insurance reset drives Philip Rivers comeback (Fox Sports) Asked afterward if he would follow his son Gunner to Raleigh, Rivers kept it short. “I don’t know that,” Rivers said to reporters in Alabama. Pressed by WRAL on a next step in the talks, he went a little further. “There could be. I think that the potential next step would involve all of those things you referenced,” Rivers said. What Rivers inherits in Raleigh after the Dave Doeren firing NC State fired Dave Doeren on Oct. 24, a day after a 31-28 loss at the Stanford Cardinal dropped the Wolfpack to 3-4, and handed the interim job to running backs coach and special teams coordinator Todd Goebbel. Doeren leaves as the winningest coach in school history at 98-74, and the school owes him $9.75 million in base salary on a contract that ran through December 2029. Goebbel’s team beat the California Golden Bears 31-10 and then lost 41-3 to the Duke Blue Devils, so Rivers takes over a 4-5 roster with the Syracuse Orange, Florida State Seminoles and North Carolina Tar Heels still to play. Rivers emerged as the favorite early in the search and met with athletic director Boo Corrigan and other NC State officials in Alabama on Nov. 4, per WRAL. Russell Wilson, another former Wolfpack quarterback, was also in discussions for the job before the search settled on Rivers. Gunner Rivers committed to NC State on Feb. 23 and is ranked 168th in the SC Next 300, though his senior season at St. Michael ended with a knee injury. Dec 14, 2025; Seattle, Washington, USA; Indianapolis Colts head coach Shane Steichen, left, talks with quarterback Philip Rivers (17) during a second quarter timeout against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Ng-Imagn Images Philip Rivers threw for 13,484 yards and 95 touchdowns at NC State from 2000 to 2003 under Chuck Amato, who died last month at 80, and took the Wolfpack to four straight bowl games. The 2002 team went 11-3, still the only double-digit win season in program history, and NC State has not won an ACC title since 1979. Rivers interviewed for the Buffalo Bills head coaching job in January before withdrawing, and he came out of retirement last fall to start three games for the Indianapolis Colts af

item.title: Two French Guards Collapse As Macron Welcomes Slovak President
item.description: Two members of France’s elite Republican Guard collapsed almost simultaneously outside the Elysee Palace as President Emmanuel Macron welcomed his Slovak counterpart, according to televised images and a presidential source. As is customary for the arrival of foreign heads of state, the Republican Guards formed an honour guard in full ceremonial dress with sabres for the arrival of Slovak President Peter Pellegrini late Wednesday. One guard can be seen swaying before crashing to the ground, falling against a pillar at the Elysee Palace as his ceremonial sword clattered to the ground. France’s President Emmanuel Macron (R) bids farewell to Slovakia’s President Peter Pellegrini following their meeting at the Elysee presidential Palace in Paris on November 11, 2026. (Photo by Guillaume Saligot / AFP) | Guillaume Saligot / AFP Aides and Macron immediately rushed towards the stricken guard, images from an AFP photographer showed. Le Parisien daily said that a second guard collapsed off camera, with Macron looking concerned and then hurriedly welcoming his Slovak counterpart. A French presidential source, who asked not to be named, told AFP that both guards had suffered from “fainting attacks” and no other comment would be made. “Both of them were swiftly taken care of, and everything is fine,” added the source. The Republican Guard, part of the French gendarmerie, is responsible for guards of honour in France, which often involve standing for long periods in heavy clothing while holding their sword vertically. France’s President Emmanuel Macron (L) and other officials attend to a Republican Guard who fainted while standing at attention, as he waits the arrival of Slovakia’s President at the Elysee Palace in Paris on November 11, 2026. (Photo by Guillaume Saligot / AFP) | Guillaume Saligot / AFP AFP The post Two French Guards Collapse As Macron Welcomes Slovak President appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Miami can't let injury fear stop them from building around a mobile QB
item.description: MIAMI GARDENS ― The Miami Dolphins starting quarterback for at least the next four games had -142 rushing yards in four years of college football. So we're going to start out by suggesting this has nothing to do with young backup Kyle McCord , who demonstrated a good arm, attack mindset and confident leadership at Ohio State and Syracuse. (For the record, lost yardage by sacks count in quarterback rushing totals in college. McCord did have 240 total college rushing yards excluding sacks.) This is about Miami's long-term quarterback situation, which remains unclear. Malik Willis is a dynamic, explosive, exciting runner ― when healthy. Willis is also now sidelined following injuries to a toe, thumb, groin and core this season. Willis needs rest, at a minimum. He has not looked like himself in the last two games, after being among the league leaders in quarterback rushing yards earlier this season. "This is the best decision for him," Miami coach Jeff Hafley said. This is where we tell you that whether it's Malik Willis or some other unknown quarterback, the best long-term decision for Miami at quarterback is to have a quarterback who can run. Most of the best teams have quarterbacks who can extend plays, escape danger, bail teammates out and earn first downs and more, on the run. And if there is a slightly higher injury risk for those quarterbacks, so be it. The upside is worth the risk. I asked Hafley how he weighs and balances the fact that mobile, athletic quarterbacks create an enormous benefit on game day, but might also face an increased risk of injury. Hafley, a defensive play-caller and long-time defensive coordinator and defensive coach, knows how much more difficult it is to game plan for and handle a mobile quarterback on game day. As for injury risk? "Some that I've been around that go through a whole season playing that way and nothing happens," Hafley said. "And some guys, they get hit and something does happen. But then you get a guy who stays in the pocket and can't get out of the way and he's getting hit even more. So I mean, I think there's a balance between a pocket quarterback and a guy who has the ability to make plays. You're going to get hit regardless." He's right. Running quarterback. Pocket quarterback. They all get hit. In some ways, being able to escape and get out of bounds or slide is a better situation than being crunched in the pocket. And yes, some pocket passers are better than others at avoiding sacks and hits. That attribute can be as important as explosive runs. Miami Dolphins can't shy away from mobile QBs And yes, it is also crucial that a successful quarterback be accurate, on time and poised. The Dolphins saw how much more challenging it was to earn first downs when Tua Tagovailoa became far less mobile and was generally encouraged not to run. Defenses played Miami differently, viewing Tua almost as a 7-foot center left completely alone at the 3-point line. The quarterbacks who have led the NFL in rushing ya

item.title: Raiders’ Klint Kubiak Goes Viral for ‘Depressed’ Reaction to Kirk Cousins Trade
item.description: Up until November, 10, Kirk Cousins was Las Vegas Raiders’ trusted starter under whom, no. 1 draft pick quarterback Fernando Mendoza was supposed to develop. But at the dying moment of the trade deadline, Minnesota Vikings offered a third round pick to the Raiders to acquire Kirk Cousins from them. The deal worked out well for the Vikings as they were in need of a quarterback but it’s not clear whether the Raiders are happy with the trade. Head coach Klint Kubiak was visibly depressed as the general manager was speaking about how the deal happened. HC Klint Kubiak seemed upset after Kirk Cousins trade Las Vegas Raiders general manager John Spytek and head coach Klint Kubiak held a joint press conference shortly after the NFL trade deadline. The session focused on why the Raiders made the move, the readiness of 2026 No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza, and the team’s outlook for the rest of the season. Feb 24, 2026; Indianapolis, IN, USA; Las Vegas Raiders general manager John Spytek speaks at the NFL Scouting Combine at the Indiana Convention Center. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images It was mostly Spytek who was vocal in most part of the press conference . Head coach Klint Kubiak sat next to him and looked visibly upset at the situation. Spytek explained how the deal happened and established that the Raiders were not shopping Cousins. “I never made one call on Kirk Cousins. I got a few phone calls, but one real one this morning,” Spytek said. The serious offer came quickly that morning from Vikings GM Nolan Teasley. “There was nothing to speak about,” Spytek said. “We didn’t have any expectation that this was coming.” Now that the veteran has returned to his former home, the no. 1 draft pick becomes the starter for the remainder of the season for the Raiders. Klint Kubiak spoke about his readiness and expressed his confidence on the rookie. Klint Kubiak feels confident about Fernando Mendoza Klint Kubiak is hopeful about the rookie’s preparation and readiness. “Fernando has done everything we ask him to do in practice. I think he’s exceeded those expectations,” Kubiak said. “He has shown us that he’s ready, not only physically but mentally,” he added. “I do… I think with the right role model, that will accelerate his growth. And we had the right role model.” Kubiak commented on how he has improved watching Kirk Cousins. The Las Vegas Raiders’ next game is against the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday. This will be Fernando Mendoza’s first career start as the Raiders’ quarterback. Even though it was a bit unexpected for Mendoza to be the starter, Kubiak thinks he is ready and has learned enough sitting for the nine games this season so far. item.title: Israeli occupation in southern Lebanon: Displaced families struggle to cope
item.description: In Lebanon, more than 360,000 people are still displaced after months of war between Israel and Hezbollah, according to the UN. Along the border, the Israeli army claims to be fighting the Iran-backed militant group but now occupies 6 percent of Lebanese territory and is wiping entire villages off the map. In the border area, we meet families living in makeshift housing. Many fear they may never go home.

item.title: Who Pep Guardiola previously named as his favourite modern NBA players post-Michael Jordan
item.description: Photo by Rob Newell - CameraSport via Getty Images Pep Guardiola is becoming a talking point in the United States amid links to the USMNT job. Mauricio Pochettino remains in charge at the time of writing but he is now being mooted to leave his role and join English team, Manchester United, who sacked their coach on Thursday. Amid speculation about Pochettino’s future, Guardiola is being talked about as a potential successor. For those unfamiliar, Pep is a former player who has cemented himself as one of the best soccer coaches in Europe, dominating with FC Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Manchester City. But while he has spent most of his life around soccer, he also has a soft spot for the NBA. As shared by Marc Stein back in August 2025, Guardiola previously said: “The NBA has always been important in my life.” Stein also shared that when speaking about the NBA, the manager ‘named Stephen Curry, Luka Doncic and LeBron James as his favourite modern players’ of the post-Michael Jordan era. All three of those stars are still going strong in the 2026/27 season, with Doncic currently having the highest average (39.3) in the division. Curry is second on that list right now (30.6) and while LeBron may not be competing with them on the points front, his Philadelphia 76ers are battling at the top end of the Eastern Conference. They have a 9-3 record before they play the Toronto Raptors on Thursday night. item.title: Liverpool forward could be set for January move despite recent performances
item.description: Liverpool forward could be set for January move despite recent performances Liverpool weigh January loan for Will Wright amid academy development push Liverpool head into the international break in decent shape, fourth in the Premier League after 10 matches, and that matters. Early work under Andoni Iraola has been solid, organised and largely sensible. Still, league position can hide a few things. This squad needs refining, and the next transfer window looks less like a luxury and more like routine maintenance. According to the Daily Mail, one of the more interesting January calls concerns not a glamorous signing, but a possible loan for academy striker Will Wright. That tells you something about where Liverpool are. Recruitment is not only about buying, it is about sequencing development properly and avoiding stagnation for younger players. Wright, 19, has built a strong case for senior football. He has 13 goals in all competitions, boosted by a hat-trick in the 5-3 win over Fenerbahce, and he has already picked up an England youth call-up. There is no mystery here. Liverpool think regular men’s football could speed up his progress, and there should be plenty of interest if they decide to send him out. That decision, sensibly, will involve Iraola. This is important because Liverpool’s current head coach has shown a willingness to use younger players. Trey Nyoni, Lewis Koumas and Luke Chambers have all had chances, and that matters more than broad slogans about pathways. A pathway only counts when minutes are actually available. Photo: IMAGO Will Wright loan could suit Liverpool and player There is also a wider structure behind this. Iraola is said to be in regular contact with academy staff, including Rob Page, Alex Inglethorpe and Luiz Fernando Iubel. That should be standard at a serious club, but it often is not. The detail about Iubel, Julian Ward and loans manager Gary Probert watching Wright’s hat-trick in Turkey suggests Liverpool are trying to make this call on evidence rather than hype. Wright’s story is straightforward. He joined from Salford City in August 2025 after making his senior debut there during the 2024/25 season. He had already featured in the EFL Trophy, FA Cup and League Two, then stepped into Liverpool’s Under 21s, scored six goals in his first campaign and later made a pre-season senior appearance against Athletic Club at Anfield. He was also named in a Premier League matchday squad in April 2026. Progress has been steady. Andoni Iraola faces practical January choices The question for Liverpool is timing. If Wright stays, he remains close to the first team and under direct supervision. If he goes, he may get the sort of repetitive competitive exposure academy football cannot replicate. That is usually where the real learning happens for a young striker, movement under pressure, poor pitches, physical centre-backs, little time to think. Liverpool also have bigger January business to consider, with squad gaps and contract

item.title: Chelsea remain interested in potential move for Arsenal midfielder
item.description: Chelsea remain interested in potential move for Arsenal midfielder Martin Zubimendi Transfer Latest as Chelsea Track Arsenal Midfielder for January Chelsea are among the clubs keeping a close watch on Martin Zubimendi before the January transfer window, with Independent reporting that the Arsenal midfielder is being monitored alongside Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid. The developing situation appears to centre on availability as much as admiration. Zubimendi arrived at Arsenal in summer 2025 in a “long-awaited £60m move from Real Sociedad” and was initially a regular under Mikel Arteta. Since then, his role has shifted. The report states the midfielder “fell out of favour towards the end of last season’s title run”, a change that has naturally alerted elite clubs searching for proven quality in the middle of the pitch. Chelsea’s interest makes obvious sense. The club continue to assess midfield balance, profile and reliability, and Zubimendi is described as “one of the few of a high level potentially available in the next window”. That line matters. January is notoriously difficult for top-end recruitment, particularly in central areas, so when a player of Zubimendi’s calibre appears even remotely obtainable, attention follows quickly. Photo IMAGO Chelsea interest grows around Arsenal midfield depth Arsenal’s internal picture is also important. Arteta “still sees him as a valuable option” but the landscape has changed after the “£85m purchase of Bruno Guimaraes in the summer”. With Declan Rice and Bruno Guimaraes now used as the main pairing and “Myles Lewis-Skelly oftern in the mix as well”, competition is fierce. Arsenal also have separate priorities, with the report adding that they “want a transitional winger – a fast player who can carry the ball up the pitch quickly”. That strategic need could shape the market. Arsenal are “unlikely to move without first making a major sale” and that has led Chelsea and the Madrid clubs to believe “a deal may be possible for Zubimendi”. Among the midfielders available to move, he is “seen as making the most sense as an outgoing”. Martin Zubimendi price and January transfer outlook If Arsenal do open the door, the valuation looks clear. It is “expected Arsenal want to recoup the £60m at least”. For Chelsea, that would represent a significant outlay in a winter market, but also one attached to an experienced international who remains highly regarded despite reduced prominence in north London. The report also notes that Zubimendi “was still a key player in a title season” and “played a significant part in the Ferran Torres goal that won Spain the World Cup in July”. His standing has not collapsed, his pathway at Arsenal has simply become more complicated. There is also a short-term fitness detail. Zubimendi is currently playing in a protective mask after suffering “a suspected broken nose” during Arsenal’s 2-0 win over Everton last month, although he has been considered fit enough to continue playing as the in

item.title: Pierre Sage leads race to become RC Lens manager; Thiago Motta also considered
item.description: Pierre Sage leads race to become RC Lens manager; Thiago Motta also considered Pierre Sage, who has not yet been relieved of his duties by Crystal Palace, is the frontrunner to take over at RC Lens, as per a report from L’Équipe . Yannick Cahuzac has been sacked by Lens after an ill-fated nine-game stint. He replaced Dino Toppmoller in September, who himself succeeded Sage in the role. The Frenchman could make a spectacular return. Contrary to a report from Fabrizio Romano, sources in France indicate that Sage would be open to taking the job at the Bollaert. In any case, he must first depart Crystal Palace, who, in order to thwart the Frenchman’s return to Les Sang et Or, could keep him on their payroll, despite taking him off his first-team managerial duties, L’Équipe understands. That could prevent a return, with Lens insisting on hiring a manager who is not under contract elsewhere. Thiago Motta, who proposed his candidacy at Olympique Lyonnais earlier this month, is also a candidate for the role at Lens. Didier Digard also remains a contender. GFFN | Luke Entwistle

item.title: 21 sixes in an innings! New Zealand batter Bevon Jacobs comes close to world record
item.description: New Zealand batter Bevon Jacobs produced a stunning batting display in the domestic Ford Trophy on Thursday, smashing an unbeaten 202 off just 137 balls against Otago in Auckland. The 21 sixes in his innings set a new record for the most sixes hit by a New Zealand batter in a List A innings. Jacobs was just two sixes short of the world record of 23, held by Australia's Da’Arcy Short. His powerful knock helped Auckland post 334/8 at the Kennards Hire Community Oval. However, Jacobs' effort went in vain as Otago chased down the target in 49.1 overs. A total of 34 sixes were hit in the match. Jacobs hits 21 sixes in record-breaking knock Batting at No. 4, Jacobs turned his maiden List A century into a double century with some powerful hitting. He reached the 200-run mark in just 137 balls, hitting seven fours and 21 sixes. The 21 sixes are the most by a New Zealand batter in a List A innings. Jacobs came close to breaking the world record, which belongs to Australia's Da’Arcy Short. Short had hit 23 sixes while scoring 257 off 148 balls for Western Australia against Queensland in Sydney in 2018. — MargotButcher (@MargotButcher) Jacobs also became only the fourth New Zealand batter to score a double century in List A cricket. He joined Jamie How (2012), Martin Guptill (2015) and Chad Bowes (2024) on the list. His 202 not out was also a record score for Auckland Aces in the Ford Trophy and the third double century in the tournament's history. — thenichecache (@thenichecache) From India series to domestic record Jacobs recently featured in New Zealand's five-match T20I series against India. He scored more than 135 runs against the world champions and followed it up with this remarkable performance in domestic cricket. The 28-year-old has also played 16 T20Is for New Zealand since making his debut in late 2024. However, he is yet to make his debut in ODIs and Test cricket.

item.title: Bruins Set To Make Uniform History Against Canadiens At TD Garden
item.description: Bruins Set To Make Uniform History Against Canadiens At TD Garden originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Thursday's meeting between the Boston Bruins and Montreal Canadiens will provide fans with considerably more than another chapter in one of hockey's greatest rivalries. The Bruins will debut their new Varsity Sweaters at TD Garden as part of a special event celebrating Boston's collegiate hockey culture. The uniforms represent a significant departure from the organization's familiar black-and-gold appearance. According to the Bruins, the new sweaters mark the first time Boston has featured an entirely brown uniform since its inaugural season in 1924. The design incorporates traditional collegiate influences while paying tribute to the franchise's extensive history. Boston plans to wear the sweaters 12 times during the 2026-27 season. Original Six Rivals Create Unique NHL Moment The Bruins and Canadiens will also become the first opponents to compete against one another while wearing their respective Hometown Remix uniforms. The collection, introduced through a partnership between the NHL and Fanatics, gives teams an opportunity to incorporate local culture into their on-ice appearance. Boston's contribution draws heavily from the city's relationship with college hockey. The “Varsity Sweater” is the #NHLBruins first all-brown uniform since its inaugural season in 1924 and includes Ivy League prep stylings that pay homage to the rich collegiate hockey landscape in Boston. 📰 Take a look back at the club's uniform history: https://t.co/inAT5d9Ti8 https://t.co/WGjzBS9W7Q — Boston Bruins (@NHLBruins) November 12, 2026 The Bruins have created a fictional institution called Causeway University to accompany the uniform launch. Thursday's festivities will resemble a college homecoming celebration, with several elements designed to transform the atmosphere inside TD Garden. The Northeastern University pep band will perform before the game and during portions of the evening. Fans attending Thursday's game will also receive Causeway University T-shirts. The Bruins have planned a special entrance for the players and additional college-themed entertainment throughout the evening. Those details should make the uniform debut a particularly memorable occasion for fans attending the rivalry game.
