item.title: Throwing cow dung: Diwali celebrations take an unusual turn in southern India
item.description: The third day of Diwali was marked in a memorable way on Wednesday in Gummatapura, a hamlet located in India's Tamil Nadu state. Local men and boys threw cow dung at each other to celebrate the festival of Gorehabba which honours Lord Beereshwara, a God worshipped by locals. Believed to be around 300 years old, the festival attracts tourists from across India and further afield.

item.title: Ex-Serie A flop Jardel opens up on drug abuse: ‘I nearly died’
item.description: Ex-Serie A flop Jardel opens up on drug abuse: ‘I nearly died’ Former Ancona striker Mario Jardel opens up on his alcohol and drug abuse: ‘I nearly died; a friend of mine saved my life.’ The former Brazilian striker played for Ancona in Serie A in the second half of the 2003-04 campaign. He joined the Italian club from Bolton in the January transfer window. Jardel about his Ancona spell: ‘Only have bad memories’ “I only have bad memories. In six months, I didn’t get paid, and I played just three matches,” the ex-striker told La Gazzetta dello Sport about his brief spell in Ancona. “The squad was packed full of players, poorly run, and went bankrupt at the end of the year. I bonded with Sonetti and Galeone, much less so with the fans. “I was 31, I was overweight, and someone called me ‘Lardel’. Probably because when they unveiled me against Perugia I saluted the wrong end: we had the same colours. Some fans took offence after that gesture,” the former striker added. BOLTON – SEPTEMBER 27: Mario Jardel of Bolton Wanderers during the FA Barclaycard Premiership match between Bolton Wanderers and Wolverhampton Wanderers held on September 27, 2003 at the Reebok Stadium, in Bolton, England. The match ended in a 1-1 draw. (Photo by Michael Steele/Getty Images) Who did advice him to go to Ancona? “Jorge Mendes. He wasn’t my agent, but a close friend,” Jardel replied. “He had contacts in Italy, mentioned my name to some agents and somehow they brought me to Ancona. I was looking for a club where I could play regularly and recover after the nightmare of missing out on the 2002 World Cup, but mentally I never recovered.” Between 2001 and 2003, Jardel had scored 67 goals in 62 appearances with Sporting CP, still not enough to earn a call-up to the Brazil national team for the 2002 World Cup, which the South Americans won. “I fell into depression and started drinking excessively,” Jardel admitted. YOKOHAMA – JUNE 30: Referee Pierluigi Collina of Italy consoles a dejected Oliver Kahn of Germany after the World Cup Final match between Germany and Brazil played at the International Stadium Yokohama, Yokohama, Japan on June 30, 2002. Brazil won the match 2-0. (Photo by Gary M. Prior/Getty Images) “Playing in a World Cup was the dream of my life. My first wife left me, and there were issues regarding the custody of our children. I felt that everything was slipping away from me, but the worst was yet to come.” But the ex-Serie A flop hadn’t yet hit rock bottom. “In the summer of 2003, I tried cocaine. I was on holiday, and I knew I could take it during that period because there was no doping control,” he said. “I liked it; it made me feel alive and not depressed. Once, I stayed awake for an entire week. Then I had an overdose; I nearly died, and a friend who was with me saved my life. That was where I hit rock bottom. “I spent months speaking with psychiatrists,” he continued. “I came out of it for good when I met my second wife, Sandra: she made me understand the m

item.title: Mike Brown points out what was ‘very alarming’ about Jalen Brunson during Knicks’ loss to Cavaliers
item.description: Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images Mike Brown noticed something about Jalen Brunson’s performance against the Cleveland Cavaliers that truly shocked him. After a strong string of recent results, the Knicks were beaten by the Cavaliers at home in a result that left many of their fans very disappointed. Despite their talent, the Cavaliers aren’t considered a strong team this season, so a loss to them isn’t a good look for the reigning world champions. Mike Brown believes Jalen Brunson deserves a ‘better whistle’ after 0-FT game Speaking after the New York Knicks’ loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers, head coach Mike Brown discussed their performance and what caused their loss. In particular, he pointed to their free-throw disparity and pointed out how a player like Jalen Brunson getting zero free-throw attempts was quite concerning. Mike Brown said: “It’s a possession game, and we lost it in the category. They had 14 more free-throw attempts than us, four more offensive rebounds, and two less turnovers. When that happens against a good team, it’s going to be hard to win the game. So, I give them a lot of credit. “I am a little surprised Jalen [Brunson] played almost 35 minutes, and he had zero free-throw attempts. That’s pretty alarming. I’m not sure how or why it was that way. I know at one time, the free-throw advantage was 18-3. “That’s not why we lost the game, but you hope you get a better whistle when you’re playing a good team like that because it’s already hard enough to go win a game. That was part of the reason why we lost the possession game.” Brunson did have a decent scoring performance, delivering 27 points, while shooting 12/27 from the field and 3/8 from beyond the arc. However, him not getting to the free-throw line does come as a surprise, as the last time he had a game with zero free-throw attempts was back in February of this year against the Philadelphia 76ers. For a player of Brunson’s offensive prowess, seeing him fail to draw a single foul in the shooting process during a game is quite startling. item.title: Lindblad and Lawson to continue at Racing Bulls
item.description: Arvid Lindblad (left) and Liam Lawson have taken Racing Bulls to fifth place in the constructors' championship on 114 points, 45 points ahead of Alpine [Getty Images] Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson will continue as the drivers for Red Bull's second team Racing Bulls in 2027. Red Bull had been deciding whether to promote Bulgarian Formula 2 front-runner Nikola Tsolov in place of Lawson but have decided to spend a second season assessing their current line-up. Team principal Alan Permane said: "I have no doubt that this is the best driver line-up for us, bringing a strong combination of experience and ambition. "Both have demonstrated their ability and potential throughout the season, and we've seen the progress they've made, both individually and as a pairing." The decision to retain both marks a break from the previous Red Bull philosophy of fast-tracking drivers through the programme. Racing Bulls essentially exists to find potential drivers for the main Red Bull team, so the company has tended to jettison drivers who have been given a chance and not succeeded. That's why Lawson, 24, was considered vulnerable. He was promoted to Red Bull alongside Max Verstappen for the 2025 season only to be demoted after just two races in which he had struggled. The New Zealander has since sought to rebuild his career and was much more convincing when he was re-promoted to Red Bull for the Dutch, Italian and Spanish Grands Prix this year while regular driver Isack Hadjar was recovering from a broken wrist. Keeping Lawson on board for 2027 gives Red Bull a known-quality benchmark with which to continue their assessment of Lindblad, who made his debut this season. The 19-year-old Briton has excelled at times in his rookie year but on average has been a little behind Lawson, who has out-qualified him 13 times to nine and has scored more than twice as many points. Lawson said: "We've had a brilliant season together and the team has worked very hard to produce a fast car, which I've loved driving. "It feels great to be part of a historic season for the team as we continue our fight for fifth place in the constructors' championship. "I'm looking forward to carrying this moment forward with Arvid through to 2027; we're building something super positive and I'm excited by what we can achieve together." Lindblad added: "It's been a truly special year, full of new experiences and learnings since the very first pre-season test. I'd like to thank everyone for their trust and support. "I can't wait to get started next year, building on everything I've learned during my rookie season." The news release announcing the pairing made no mention of Tsolov, who is expected to be retained by Red Bull in some form of reserve role in which he gains experience through work in the simulator and with testing previous cars. item.title: Ayrton Senna's 1994 Williams F1 car heads to auction with $6million estimate
item.description: Motorsport photo A Williams FW16 driven by three-time Formula 1 champion Ayrton Senna in his final season in the series is going under the hammer in New York. RM Sotheby's is offering chassis FW16B-01 in Sotheby's 'The Now & Contemporary Evening Auction', with an estimate of $4million to $6million (£2.95million to £4.45million). It is the first time the car has been put up for public sale. When the Brazilian driver joined Williams from McLaren in 1994, the Grove outfit agreed that he would receive one of its chassis if it won that year's constructors' championship. Senna tragically died at the 1994 San Marino Grand Prix, in chassis FW16-02. Williams went on to beat Benetton to the constructors' crown, while Damon Hill lost the drivers' title to Michael Schumacher by a single point. At the end of the year, the team kept its word and gave FW16B-01 to Senna's family. According to RM Sotheby's, it is one of only two surviving FW16s that Senna drove, although he never raced the chassis himself. It was the spare car at the season-opening Brazilian Grand Prix, but Senna took it out for the race-day warm-up at Interlagos and set a quicker time than Schumacher, who went on to win. 🏎️ AUTOMOVILISMO / F1 | Subastan el histórico Williams FW16B-01 que Ayrton Senna manejó en 1994. El monoplaza saldrá a la venta el 16 de noviembre en Nueva York con una base millonaria. https://t.co/CtXODCJASF — Tiempo Extra (@TiempoExtraAr) November 9, 2026 Days later, he and Hill shared it in testing at Jerez, covering 842km across three sessions. The Senna family owned the FW16B-01 from 1994 until 2024, with the car kept in Williams's care. The current owner bought it privately through RM Sotheby's. It has never been restored. "Chassis FW16B-01 remained completely untouched for the following 30 years, with a notable exception being the addition of Senna’s personal seat, and is today presented in totally preserved, unrestored condition," the auction listing states. "Acquired by the current owner in 2024 having been purchased from the Senna family via RM Sotheby’s, it has remained preserved and unused since." item.title: Sam Reinhart: One of the Most Prolific Players in Florida Panthers History
item.description: Jonathan Huberdeau and Sam Reinhart only played together with the Florida Panthers for one season but for the past couple of days, they were linked together once more. The two had been tied for second-most goals scored in franchise history ever since Reinhart got No. 198 last Wednesday against the Blackhawks. On Tuesday night in Columbus, Reinhart has second place to himself after scoring No. 199. Sasha Barkov is the franchise leader with 286. He may not be caught. If he does, it will probably be Reinhart who does it, though. “It’s obviously pretty special, but, probably still behind ‘Cap’ in every other category I’m sure,” Reinhart said after Florida’s 4-1 win over the Blue Jackets on Tuesday. When Huberdeau was traded to Calgary in 2022, he left town as the team’s all-time leader in games played, points and assists. Barkov had already become the team’s all-time leader in goals scored when he passed Olli Jokinen with No. 189 in 2021. In the years since, Barkov and Aaron Ekblad have overtaken Huberdeau for the games-played mark, with Barkov taking the assists lead as well. Barkov also owns the franchise record for points with 782. Huberdeau had 613 which will remain second at least for the foreseeable future: Ekblad has 413 and Reinhart 403. And, Paul Maurice said Reinhart’s impact is not just scoring goals. “More than you see on the ice,” he said. “Everything that comes out of his mouth on the bench is just bang on. His compete level is so high, moving to the middle of the ice and he has still been prolific for us.’’ When the Panthers pulled off a blockbuster deal for Reinhart at the 2021 NHL Draft, they were expecting an impact player — but he has proved to be much more. Since joining the Panthers, Reinhart leads all players in goals (199) and points (403), leading the team in scoring in three of his first five seasons including the past three. This year, Reinhart is tied for the team lead with 10 goals; his 18 points ranks fourth. In the playoffs, Reinhart has been exceptional. In 2024, Reinhart helped the Panthers secure their first Stanley Cup championship by breaking a 1-1 tie against Edmonton in Game 7 of the Final by scoring on a pass from Carter Verhaeghe . That season, Reinhart led Florida with 57 goals during the regular season — then scored 10 more in the playoffs. The following year, Reinhart helped Florida thump the Oilers in Game 6 and win the Cup again by scoring four times in a 5-1 win. It was the first playoff hat trick in Panthers history and the first four-goal Stanley Cup Final game since Maurice Richard in 1957. Reinhart had seven goals in the 2025 Final and 11 in the playoffs. He also had other big playoff moments such as beating the Rangers in OT of Game 4 of the 2024 Eastern Conference Final. In 2023, he won Game 3 against the Maple Leafs in overtime as well. item.title: Smith's Netherlands switch sad - SA swimming boss
item.description: Tatjana Smith won one gold and one silver medal at both the Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024 Olympic Games [Getty Images] The decision by South Africa's most decorated Olympian Tatjana Smith to switch allegiance to the Netherlands is "sad" for the nation, says Swimming South Africa CEO Zikie Molusi. Double Olympic champion Smith, who has dual citizenship because her father is Dutch, was in tears when she announced her decision on Wednesday. She said that the opportunity "offers greater high-performance support" and that South African athletes "deserve a system that gives them an opportunity to thrive, not just survive". "When I received that correspondence from Tatjana we understood because she has been really generous and kind enough to articulate the rationale that informed the decision," Molusi, the acting CEO of the governing body, told eNews Channel Africa: "A very sad decision for the country, particularly as we were preparing to take the team to Beijing for the short course World Championships in December." Tearful Smith switches allegiance to Netherlands Smith, formerly Schoenmaker, previously said financial worries, which included a dispute with Swimming South Africa over prize money, contributed to her decision to step away from the sport after the Paris 2024 Olympics. The 29-year-old, who has won four Olympic medals, came out of retirement in September and is set to represent the Netherlands for the first time at the World Championships from 1-6 December. Smith said representing the Netherlands would give her "the potential to build a more sustainable career". She said the "financial and practical challenges of swimming were among the reasons my previous career became difficult to sustain". Speaking to Radio 702, Molusi accepted that Swimming South Africa should not have withheld prize money from Smith following the 2023 World Championships. Molusi said that was caused by conflicting sponsorship agreements but it "shouldn't have happened". Of the 21 athletes competing for South Africa at the Worlds next month, Molusi said "probably 50% will be subsidised fully", with the rest receiving partial support. "It's an ecosystem issue within South African sport that possibly needs to be dealt with," Molusi said. "This comes as a result of the inadequate funding that sport federations are receiving."

item.title: European tech buyers add digital sovereignty to cyber shopping list
item.description: European tech buyers are increasingly choosing cybersecurity vendors from their own continent in a bid to reduce their reliance on American technology. Digital sovereignty isn't only prompting enterprise customers to question their clouds of choice, it is also reshaping other parts of the industry too, and the shift is marked. According to sales figures compiled by Context, distributor sales in EMEA of cybersecurity products from EU-headquartered vendors jumped 35 percent in the two years to calendar Q3 2026. Total cybersecurity sales grew up 10 percent over the same period, and sales by US-run companies went up just 8 percent. That growth is from a relatively small base, though EU vendors gained nearly three percentage points to reach 15 percent of tracked sales by value. There is still a long way to go as US-headquartered vendors accounted for 62 percent. The trend coincides with a loss of trust in the Trump administration among customers outside of America, after it cosied up to autocratic rulers while criticizing and punishing allies with tariffs and more. Context stopped short of assigning blame. It said organizations are reviewing their reliance on third-party tech in light of EU compliance regimes: the NIS2 Directive and Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA). NIS2, transposed into national law in October 2024 , requires organizations in the bloc to raise their common level of security in the face of digital threats and risks to critical infrastructure. DORA, introduced in January last year, is designed to strengthen cyber security in the financial sector. "Digital sovereignty is becoming a buying decision. As customers and resellers get clearer about what it means in practice, they're asking who holds the encryption keys, who can access sensitive logs and where that data is stored," said Context veep of research Joe Turner. "We're seeing a measurable shift in the EMEA channel. EU vendors gained nearly three points of sales share in two years. An organization can keep its existing identity platform and still choose a European supplier to manage its security logs. That's the kind of decision that gives European vendors an opening." The stats indicate that EU-HQd vendors comprised 92 percent of tracked sales in security awareness training, 82 percent in vulnerability management, and 52 percent for SIEM and log management. US-headquartered companies held into 74 percent of identity and access management sales and 54 percent of cloud security sales. The Reg has asked Context for UK-specific figures to see whether British customers are also voting with their wallets for European alternatives. That certainly isn’t the case for tech purchases in the British public sector, despite Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s professed desire to buy British. Data released yesterday by the Institute for Public Policy Research showed just £1 in every £6 spent by government with the biggest technology suppliers goes to Brit businesses. Nvidia board meets over Jensen Huang’s future after affair revelations
item.description: CEO Jensen Huang’s future with Nvidia was unclear Thursday as the chip giant’s board was reported to have met after revelations he had two extramarital affairs, including with a woman accused of spying for China. The scandal has sent shares of the multi-trillion dollar behemoth plunging and left uncertain the fate of Huang, who has been a key promoter of the artificial intelligence boom. Huang, 63, has spent years lobbying against curbs on sales of advanced AI chips to China, and US President Donald Trump last year cleared Nvidia’s H200 chips for export there over objections from Beijing’s critics in both parties. The chip giant’s board met on Wednesday to weigh Huang’s future, according to CNN and the New York Times. Nvidia has not made any statements about the outcome of the meeting. Beijing has rejected the spying allegations. Nvidia shares were down around 25 percent from their all-time high in early October and the scandal has raised questions over who could replace Huang if he is ousted. The rapidly unfolding story exploded after reports that Huang, who has been married to Lori Huang for over 40 years, was involved in an extramarital romance. The Nvidia CEO has since admitted to having an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, who was a senior executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this past spring alleging Alice Huang was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. Alice Huang was among the attendees at a dinner hosted by Jensen Huang at a Chinese restaurant in Taipei on May 22, 2025, during Computex, the island’s top tech expo. At one point, Jensen Huang can be seen putting his arm around Alice Huang as she kisses him on the right cheek, press livestreams show. She visited Taiwan a total of eight times in 2024 and 2025, a Taiwanese government minister said Thursday. Nvidia’s board had already announced on Sunday a probe of what it called reporting that Jensen Huang had been the target of a “foreign intelligence effort”. Then came on Wednesday New York Times reporting that the Nvidia co-founder was involved in a second extramarital affair, saying there was video evidence of the 63-year-old executive being affectionate with Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell. Powell, 48, has been a public face of Nvidia’s efforts to expand the chip technology into higher education and health care, and was speaking at a San Jose, California conference where they “were seen being affectionate at the hotel” by bystanders, the Times reported. The chip giant’s code of conduct tells associates to avoid conflicts of interest, and cites the example of “personal relationships”. “We avoid situations where our actions might create a conflict — actual or potential — between our personal gain and our obligations to Nvidia”, the code says. – Possible ouster – Nvidia’s bylaws require a majority of the 11 board directors to remove Huang as CEO. The organised labour appreciated workers, pensioners and affiliate unions for their support, cooperation and peaceful conduct during the industrial action. “The organised labour expresses its profound appreciation to all affiliate unions, workers, pensioners and members for their unwavering solidarity, cooperation and exemplary conduct throughout the three-day sympathy strike in support of the Nigeria Union of Local Government Employees (NULGE), Osun Council. “We commend all members for their commitment, discipline, unity and peaceful conduct during the industrial action. “Your solidarity has once again demonstrated the strength of the labour movement and our collective resolve to defend workers’ rights, welfare and dignity. “Accordingly, all workers are hereby directed to resume work at midnight Nov. 11. “All affiliate unions and their members are enjoined to comply fully with this directive and return to their respective workplaces,” it said. The organised labour urged workers to remain calm, united and steadfast, while maintaining mobilisation and remaining on standby for further directives. item.title: Rockstar workers vote on union recognition as GTA VI launch looms
item.description: More than 1,600 Rockstar Games employees in the UK will begin voting on union recognition on Thursday, with the ballot kicking off just a week before the long-awaited launch of Grand Theft Auto VI. The ballot, which opens on November 12 and runs until November 26, will determine whether Rockstar formally recognizes the Rockstar Game Workers Union, part of the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain (IWGB). Nearly all UK employees below director level are eligible to vote. If successful, the union would become the largest recognized union in the UK games industry, giving workers a collective voice. The proposed recognition agreement follows four months of negotiations between Rockstar management and employees. It would allow workers to negotiate over pay, overtime, pensions, bonuses, leave and other employment conditions, while securing consultation rights over HR policies and AI. The vote comes at a particularly busy time for Rockstar, with GTA VI finally due to arrive on November 19, more than 13 years after its predecessor. The game is expected to be one of the biggest entertainment launches in history, although the people responsible for making it have rather more immediate concerns than sales records. "I am incredibly proud of the work we've put into making this game. I'm also proud of the union we've built here. For me, those two things are connected," said Nestor Uriate, an animation programmer and Rockstar Game Workers Union representative. "We care deeply about the games we make, and we want to make sure we can continue doing that work in an environment where we're respected, have a meaningful say over our conditions and can feel secure about our futures." The vote follows a year of bad blood between Rockstar and the IWGB. The union accused the GTA developer of union busting after it fired 31 members in October 2025, claiming they had been singled out for taking part in a private Discord group. Rockstar denied the allegations, insisting the workers were dismissed for gross misconduct rather than their union activities. The dispute subsequently reached an employment tribunal, where Rockstar unsuccessfully attempted to have blacklisting allegations struck from the case . Closing submissions are expected on November 17 and 18, meaning the legal proceedings will reach their final stages just as GTA VI prepares to hit shelves. Despite the ongoing dispute, Rockstar's head of publishing, Jennifer Kolbe, recently indicated that management would respect the outcome of the recognition vote, telling Bloomberg : "We go where the team goes. So if they want a union, they will have a union." The union campaign has also attracted support from elsewhere in the games industry, including SAG-AFTRA and the Communications Workers of America (CWA), which represents workers at Blizzard. Alex Marshall, president of the IWGB, said the vote was an opportunity for Rockstar employees to take greater control over their working conditions. "What happens at Rockstar

item.description: It is built of wood, resembles an Ikea and its power is totally renewable. Plus, it was built with the local community in mind. Is this facility in Falun the best datacentre in the world? ‘It was pretty cool, when they were building it. It looked like a very large Ikea,” says John Wernvik, of EcoDataCenter. He is giving me a tour of their facility in Falun, Sweden, which could lay claim to being the world’s greenest datacentre – although to many, that is a contradiction in terms. One difference is immediately visible: this datacentre is made out of wood. Huge panels of cross-laminated timber arrived at the site pre-cut, and were assembled by crane according to instructions, like flatpack furniture. Aesthetically, this section of the datacentre is more like an Ikea before the fit-out, a cavernous, echoey, immaculately clean hangar. The wood is not EcoDataCenter’s only claim to sustainability; it is more than just cosmetic, says Wernvik, the company’s chief external relations and sustainability officer. “Compared with a traditional datacentre built with steel and concrete, we lower the embodied carbon of the full structure by three times.” With a complex the size of a football pitch, that is a lot of wood, but, says Wernvik, “the amount of timber one of our datacentres uses takes the Swedish forest about 10 to 15 minutes to grow back”. Continue reading...

item.title: Sales Hack Conference 2026: Nnamani leads six industry experts to Abuja
item.description: By Chioma Okoye The Convener of the Sales Hack Conference, Chinedu Paul Nnamani, is set to bring together six professionals from the business, technology, entrepreneurship, media and management sectors for the 2026 edition of the conference scheduled to hold in Abuja on Saturday, November 14. The conference, themed “Explosive Sales: Market Smart, Convert More, Earn Big,” is aimed at equipping entrepreneurs, business owners, marketers and sales professionals with practical strategies for improving sales performance, attracting customers and growing sustainable businesses. The event is expected to attract business owners, corporate professionals, students and other stakeholders for discussions on sales strategies, market positioning, customer psychology and business growth. According to the organisers, the conference is designed to provide a platform for sharing practical business knowledge, professional experience and industry insights to help individuals and organisations strengthen their sales capabilities. The 2026 edition will feature speakers drawn from different areas of the business and professional ecosystem. They include Dr. Jamie Pajoel, Founder and Global President of Jamie Pajoel International; Kel Armstrong Amobi, Founder and Host of KaaTruths Podcast; Dr. Ninnah Samuel, a business and technology law expert; Ajah Excel, Chief Executive Officer of Silicon Africa and Convener of SMfest; and Abraham Ofure Orukpe, a business management consultant and coach. Nnamani will also feature as convener, coordinating the engagement between the speakers and participants. The organisers said the diversity of the speakers was intended to provide participants with perspectives on different aspects of sales development, including business strategy, technology, communication, consumer behaviour, legal considerations and management. Discussions will focus on practical sales techniques, buying behaviour, customer acquisition and retention, relationship building, revenue generation and strategies for competing in an increasingly demanding marketplace. The conference is also expected to provide networking opportunities for entrepreneurs, corporate professionals and emerging talents to establish business relationships and explore potential collaborations. The organisers said the event would be particularly relevant to Nigerian businesses navigating changing consumer expectations, increasing market competition and the need to develop sustainable revenue streams. The conference will hold at Centre Point Event Centre, Centre Shehu Shagari Way, Wuse, Abuja, beginning at 8 a.m. West Africa Time. Registration is available under four categories: Basic, N5,000; Executive, N15,000; Premium, N30,000; and VIP, N70,000. Further information and registration are available through the conference’s official website. The organisers said the event was part of efforts to promote knowledge sharing, professional development and improved sales capabilities among Nigerian business

item.title: Updated: Manchester United sack coach Carrick
item.description: Manchester United sacked manager Michael Carrick on Thursday after their worst-ever start to a Premier League campaign, with USA boss Mauricio Pochettino expected to replace him. Former United midfielder Carrick led the team to an impressive third-place finish last season but they have taken just eight points from 10 games in the current campaign and are mired in the relegation zone. “Manchester United can confirm that Michael Carrick has departed his role as men’s first-team head coach,” the club said in a statement. It added: “After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.” Carrick’s final game in charge was a chaotic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday, after which he stressed he would not walk away and was looking to the international break as usual. But the United hierarchy have decided to act in the hope of saving their season after a paltry three wins in all competitions. Former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain boss Pochettino would have an enormous task on his hands to revive a club that has never recovered from the departure of Alex Ferguson 13 years ago. The Red Devils, once the dominant force in English football, have been overtaken by Manchester City, Liverpool and Arsenal. United’s next game is against fierce rivals Liverpool at Anfield on November 22. The post Updated: Manchester United sack coach Carrick appeared first on Vanguard News .

Obi is presently the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate for the 2027 election. ‎ ‎These defections have triggered renewed debate about the cohesion of the political movement that emerged around Obi’s 2023 presidential campaign. 2027: IGP warns officers against compromise Thugs attack Pantami’s campaign rally in Gombe ‎ ‎While Obi continues to command a loyal support base across the country, the departure of several high-profile associates underscores the challenge of maintaining political unity and building a durable structure ahead of the next electoral cycle. ‎ However, his present alliance with Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, the leader of Kwankwasiyya Movement, is seen by many as a plus to him. ‎ ‎Below are five of such most prominent names. ‎ ‎ YUNUSA TANKO tanko yunusa ‎ ‎Perhaps the latest and most symbolic departure is that of Yunusa Tanko, who served as National Coordinator of the Obidient Movement and was one of the most visible defenders of Obi after the 2023 election. ‎ ‎Tanko was a key mobiliser of Obi’s support base across the country and regularly represented the movement on national television and at political events. item.title: Orbit Global Menu: A working global menu addon for GNOME
item.description: A new extension brings a working global menu bar to the GNOME desktop, even for some apps that don’t have menu bars at all. Orbit Global Menu is a new GNOME extension that gives the GNOME desktop a feature it was intentionally designed without, and one that some users miss very badly – this vulture being one of them. It adds a working global menu bar to the GNOME top panel. We suspect this is something that will cause strongly contrasting opinions among many GNOME users: some will by puzzled why anyone would bother, while others may think "at last!" and rush to try it. There have been other attempts to do this before, and the Reg FOSS desk has tried several of them, but we never found one that worked with the majority of applications. Our fondness for this UI feature was visible in the two-part series we wrote in September on how to customize Xfce and then in part two how to get the global menu working with more apps. The problem is getting worse over time, as in recent versions (since GNOME 40 and Gtk4), the GNOME human-interface guidelines encourage smartphone-style hamburger menus, replacing the traditional horizontal menu bar. It is tricky to add global menu bar support to apps that lack a menu bar, but Orbit's developer "Unmade" found a rather labor-intensive solution. The menu bar applet contains maps of keyboard controls for 292 different apps, so it can show a menu all on its own and then send those apps simulated keystrokes to operate it. It's not the programs' full menu trees, just a subset of them, but it works. It's also not the most elegant solution, but it is a solution and it works. We tried it on Ubuntu 26.10 and every app in the full install worked to at least some extent. If you are willing and able to build and install a small additional connector, it lets the global-menu applet talk to lots more applications. The GNOME shell is unusual among open source desktop environments, to an extent that we have criticized before. GNOME Shell was designed with a distinctive look and feel of its own, unlike almost all other desktops. It has a minimalist, stripped-down layout that doesn't look or work quite like anything else, and it's intentionally not very customizable. To change how GNOME works means writing new Javascript code, then packaging it as an extension that users can install from the GNOME Extensions website. This requires both a browser extension and a "native host messaging" connector to be installed into the underlying OS – or a purpose-written app. By default, the desktop comes with neither. The end result is that GNOME lends a visual identity to the Linux desktop, one that is clear and distinct from either Windows or macOS. (Back in 2013, this vulture argued that when Microsoft threatened to sue multiple Linux vendors over infringing Windows UI patents, some 20 years ago, this UI fragmentation was just what the company wanted .) GNOME 2 was the Linux world's default desktop. GNOME Shell was controversial in its early days,

item.title: Angola celebrates 51st independence anniversary, acknowledges Nigeria’s support
item.description: The Angola Embassy in Nigeria has commended Nigeria’s support for the country’s independence, attained in 1975. Dr José Zau, Angola’s Head of Mission to Nigeria, Benin, Niger and ECOWAS, said this at the celebration of the 51st anniversary of independence on Wednesday night in Abuja. Zau described relations between the two countries as a strategic, historic and fraternal partnership, anchored in political alignment as leading African oil producers. He said Nigeria played a significant role in supporting Angola’s independence process and the consolidation of the Angolan state. “Through the Bilateral Joint Commission, the two nations have been updating and expanding dozens of agreements and memoranda of understanding. “These cover trade, transport, culture, professional training, defence and public order, cybersecurity, and academic exchange,” he said. He cited a visa-exemption agreement for holders of diplomatic and official passports, and twinning partnerships between Angolan provinces and Nigerian states, as measures to deepen ties. The twinning pairs the Namibe and Bengo provinces with the Bayelsa and Nasarawa states, he said. He said relations were strengthened by engagement between Angolan President João Lourenço and Nigerian President Bola Tinubu. Zau said the Caculo Cabaça Dam would become operational in June 2027, with the capacity to generate at least 2,172 megawatts (MW). He said the dam would raise Angola’s total capacity from 6,400 MW to about 8,600 MW. He also highlighted the country’s achievements in 2026. (NAN) The post Angola celebrates 51st independence anniversary, acknowledges Nigeria’s support appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Erdogan Urges Return To Diplomacy To End Iran-US Conflict
item.description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan on Thursday said diplomacy should resume “without further delay” to end the US-Iran war after talks with his Iranian counterpart. Erdogan met Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the UN climate conference in the Turkish province of Antalya, his office said. During their discussion, Erdogan underscored “the importance of getting to the negotiating table without further delay” and said Turkey would continue to support efforts aimed at securing peace. “Common ground for agreement must be strengthened and diplomacy given a chance,” he said, expressing hope that the conflict with the US “would end as soon as possible”. The Middle East war broke out on February 28 with US-Israeli strikes that killed Iran’s supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Iran responded by launching missiles and drones at countries across the region, while the militant groups it backs in Lebanon, Yemen and Iraq also entered the fray. Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian leaves after delivering a speech during the High-Level Segment for Heads of States and Government at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) at the Antalya Expo Center in Antalya on November 11, 2026. Photo by OZAN KOSE / AFP In an address to the UN climate summit on Wednesday, Pezeshkian accused the United States and Israel of inflicting severe environmental damage during attacks on the Islamic Republic. “The recent criminal and illegal aggression against Iran by America and the Zionist regime… has inflicted severe damage on the environment, releasing massive quantities of pollutants and greenhouse gases into the atmosphere,” he said. Diplomatic efforts led by Qatar and Pakistan have sought to negotiate an end to the war. Tehran wants Washington to accept a raft of demands including unfreezing assets and lifting sanctions in return for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, the vital energy conduit it has blockaded since the start of the conflict. AFP The post Erdogan Urges Return To Diplomacy To End Iran-US Conflict appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: 2027: APC Is Working Towards Coronation, Not Election, ADC Ologbondiyan On Court Voiding Atiku’s Candidacy
item.description: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has described the court’s voidance of its principal presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, as an attempt to silence the voices of opposition parties, alleging that the ruling party, the All Progressives Congress (APC), was working to present its candidate, Bola Tinubu, as the sole candidate in the coming 2027 general elections. Justice Lifu, on November 5, nullified the David Mark-led leadership of the ADC and declared invalid the actions taken by the caretaker committee. The ruling followed a suit filed by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former National Deputy Chairman of the party, who challenged the process through which Mark and other members of the committee assumed leadership after the resignation of former National Chairman, Ralph Nwosu. The court’s decision was reported to have affected the process that produced Atiku as the party’s presidential candidate, as the Mark-led committee organised the primary election. The ADC, however, rejected the judgment, describing it as legally indefensible and accusing the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of seeking to weaken the opposition. The party also said it would challenge the decision, citing an earlier judgment by Justice Musa Liman of the same Federal High Court, which it said had affirmed the legitimacy of the Mark-led leadership. A combo of NDC Lawyer, Kalu Kalu, and Atiku Abubakar. Speaking further on ADC’s standpoint on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief on Thursday, Kola Ologbondiyan, Spokesperson of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, accused the APC of working toward coronating Tinubu in 2027 instead of allowing for healthy competition. Ologbondiyan alleged that the APC has given no room for opposition politics. “So it now goes into what we have been saying because what we now want is that no candidate must stand against during the election, and that goes to nothing as far as we are concerned in the African Democratic Congress.” The ADC’s Spokesperson said that his party has taken the necessary steps to appeal the judgement. “We are sure that we will go to the next level in the administration of justice; we believe that all this manipulation and attempt to suppress Nigerians, all this move to dismantle democratic structures will not work. We have seen it over and over again; it will not stand.” He alleged that the APC is working to ensure that the ADC candidate, Abubakar, is not on the ballot for the 2027 election, and to enthrone President Tinubu as a life president. “I want Nigerians to know, anyone thinking that this is about ADC is not reading the processes well. It is about one man who wants to turn himself into a life president” Ologbondiyan argued that the ADC has a subsisting decision from the Federal High Court in Abuja, a court with the same jurisdiction, earlier recognising the leadership of Senator David Mark as chairman of ADC. “The Federal High Court in Abuja here, saying, recognising the leadership of Senator David Mark as chairman

item.title: Tanuki: Pon’s Summer review – an adorable raccoon mends the world, one parcel at a time
item.description: Nintendo Switch/2, PlayStation 4/5, Xbox One/series X/S, PC; Denkiworks/Inpleron Limited This gentle game of fixing and fetching, in which you play as a furry post office worker on a BMX, has a slow, calming magic that delights in routine and restoration Arriving alongside November’s blue wave , Tanuki: Pon’s Summer is a game of quiet restoration that feels perfectly suited to the current moment. Tasked with repairing an ancient shrine in the weeks leading up to a local festival, you’ll find yourself cleaning out trash, mending broken arches and slowly bringing a small rural community back together. It sounds a bit like JL Carr’s compact but enchanting novel A Month in the Country , except instead of shell-shocked veterans of the first world war you’re left exploring the rich inner life of a Japanese racoon dog who can ride a BMX. Even so, the mixture of steady progress and general low stakes proves intoxicating. This is a short game, but it’s hard not to linger over it. Continue reading...

item.title: Travelling to the UAE from Nigeria in 2027? Here’s What You Should Know About Tourist Visas Before You Fly
item.description: Planning a trip to Dubai in 2027? You are not alone. Every year, more and more travellers add the UAE to their holiday list. Some go for the beaches, some for the shopping, and others just want to see the famous Burj Khalifa up close. But before you book your flight, there is one important thing to take care of first, your visa. The good news is that getting a UAE tourist visa is easier than it used to be. Most of the process happens online, and your visa comes straight to your email. Still, the rules are not the same for every traveller. Some people get a visa on arrival, while others must apply before they fly. A few small mistakes can also slow things down or even get your application rejected. So let us walk through what you really need to know before you pack your bags. Do Nigerian Travellers Need a Visa for the UAE? Yes, Nigerian travellers need a visa to enter the United Arab Emirates for tourism. The UAE lets travellers from some countries enter without a visa, or get one when they land. But Nigeria is not on that list. If you hold a Nigerian passport, you must apply for your UAE tourist visa before you fly. That means you cannot just show up at Dubai International Airport and sort things out there. Your visa must be approved and in your inbox before you check in for your flight. The process is not hard, though. With the right documents and a trusted service, most people get through it without any stress. Whether this is your first trip or your fifth, this guide will help you from start to finish. UAE Tourist Visa Types: Picking the Right One for Your Trip The UAE offers a few tourist visa options. The right one for you depends on how long you plan to stay and how often you want to come and go. Here are the most common choices: Visa Type Best For 14-day visa Short trips, stopovers, quick city breaks 30-day visa Regular holidays, medium-length stays 60-day visa Longer vacations, family visits, extended stays Each visa comes with its own rules. Some let you enter only once. Others let you come and go many times. The validity period also changes from one visa to another. For example, a visa might be valid for 60 days, but it may only let you stay for 30 days inside the country. Always read the details before you book your flight. How the Application Process Actually Works Applying for a UAE tourist visa in 2027 is almost all digital. You no longer need to post papers or wait in long embassy lines. Online platforms like VisaTop.com have made the whole thing easier. You can now apply from your home, your office, or even your phone. The process usually has three simple steps. Step 1: Gather Your Documents At a minimum, you will need: A clear scanned copy of your passport (valid for at least six months beyond your travel dates) A recent passport-sized photo that meets the rules You may also be asked for: Hotel booking confirmation Return flight tickets Bank statements or proof of funds Travel insurance details Step 2: Submit and Pay Once your pa

item.title: Indonesian Vice President Resigns In High School Diploma Scandal
item.description: Indonesia’s vice president resigned Thursday, undone by a scandal over his high school diploma that has added to pressure on a government facing widespread dissatisfaction over the economy, graft and wildfires. There had been repeated calls for Gibran Rakabuming Raka, 39, to step down following a Supreme Court ruling last month to annul his high school qualification, obtained abroad. On Thursday, he submitted his resignation to President Prabowo Subianto and to parliament. Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka (C) arrives at the vice president’s palace after submitting his resignation letter to the People’s Consultative Assembly in Jakarta on November 12, 2026. Photo by ABIMANYU / AFP Prabowo told reporters he had accepted Gibran’s resignation “with a heavy heart” and praised him for acting “for a greater cause, for the interests of the nation, the state, and the people of Indonesia”. “He certainly feels that he has pursued his education through an orderly process, but we all understand that the education system abroad is different from the education system in Indonesia,” the president said. Indonesia’s vice president does not have many constitutionally defined powers apart from acting as the president’s representative at official events and taking over if his boss is incapacitated. ‘Political realignment’ Gibran’s downfall came after thousands of Indonesians took to the streets in recent weeks to protest economic hardship, graft, perceived authoritarianism and the government’s handling of months of devastating wildfires emitting toxic haze. University students protest demanding a government review including lowering the prices of basic commodities, military involvement in civilian affairs, free meal program, taxation of sanitary pads and addressing the issue of wildfires in Surabaya on November 10, 2026. (Photo by Juni KRISWANTO / AFP) | Juni KRISWANTO / AFP His exit is likely to complicate a loose governing alliance that includes the parties of Prabowo and of his predecessor Joko Widodo — Gibran’s father, who goes by Jokowi. The resignation “marks a significant political realignment, but does not necessarily threaten government stability”, according to Khairul Fahmi, executive director of the Institute for Security and Strategic Studies (ISESS) think tank. “Jokowi will retain political influence, but Gibran’s departure could reduce his network’s direct access to power. For Prabowo, this creates greater room to consolidate his leadership and pursue his own political agenda,” Khairul told AFP. Two years into his term, Prabowo’s popularity has reached record lows. Last week, Indonesian authorities arrested the former national police chief and three senior police officials for allegedly tapping the president’s telephone. On Thursday, police said they were investigating possible treason. Prabowo’s rise to power was widely credited to support from the popular Jokowi, who served two terms from 2014 to 2024. item.title: London hotel put admin login for booking website on whiteboard behind the front desk
item.description: Welcome, once again, to PWNED, where all the victims are self-owned. This week, we welcome you to a London hotel where you could check out its admin credentials for a booking website just by walking past the front desk. Our story comes courtesy of Neycho Tepavicharov, co-founder of Flashcloud, a Delaware-based web hosting company. He was staying at a hotel in London when he noticed a shocking breach of basic security protocols by management, who were a little too hospitable with their credentials. As he was passing through the lobby, Tepavicharov noticed that the door behind the front desk was open and, inside that back room, there was a whiteboard. On the whiteboard, written in plain English, were the hotel’s Booking.com administrative username and password. Anyone near the desk could clearly see the login information, and if they didn’t have time to write it down, they could have snapped a picture for later use. As Tepavicharov explains, there’s plenty of mischief you could perform with these credentials. “With that login, someone could change or cancel reservations, see guests’ names and contact details, or message guests pretending to be the hotel,” he said. “Fake 'please confirm your payment' messages sent from compromised hotel accounts are a well-known scam.” An attacker could potentially exploit that access to disrupt hotel operations or target guests with convincing scams. Whether the exposed credentials alone would have been enough to access the account would depend on its security settings. Tepavicharov decided to play the role of good samaritan and warn the hotel’s manager that the business was endangering itself by showing everyone its password. “I asked to speak with the manager and showed him what I’d seen. He was mortified and very grateful,” Tepavicharov said. “Nobody on staff had thought of it as a risk. It was just the easiest way for the whole team to share one login.” After Tepavicharov talked to the manager, not only did the hotel change its ways, but it also moved its website to his hosting service, Flashcloud. Tepavicharov notes that there are plenty of takeaways from this incident. Most important: give each user dedicated credentials with their own separate login, and use multi-factor authentication. “The lesson is an old one, but it keeps happening,” he said. “Shared logins end up written somewhere convenient. Give each staff member their own login, turn on two-factor authentication, and keep passwords in a password manager, not on the wall.” ®

item.title: Nvidia preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang: US media
item.description: Nvidia’s board is preparing to oust its co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang, US media reported Wednesday, as the chip giant’s chief faces new accusations of infidelity, after revelations he had an affair with a woman accused of spying for China. The tech company’s board was preparing to meet as soon as Wednesday to determine Huang’s future, according to the Wall Street Journal, which quoted people familiar with the matter. The New York Times reported Wednesday that Huang was also involved in a second extramarital affair, with a subordinate, saying there was video evidence of the 63-year-old executive being affectionate with Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell. Powell, 48, has been a public face of Nvidia’s efforts to expand the chip technology into higher education and health care, and was speaking at a San Jose, California conference where they “were seen being affectionate at the hotel” by bystanders, the Times reported. The report of the second affair follows Huang’s acknowledgment of a relationship with Alice Huang, a senior executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. The Wall Street Journal reported that the two were photographed together in Taipei in 2024 and 2025. US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this past spring alleging Alice Huang was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. The Nvidia CEO admitted to having had a relationship with Huang — to whom he bears no familial relation — in a note to Nvidia employees Sunday, writing: “I was unfaithful to my wife.” The same day Nvidia’s board of directors said in a statement that they’d launched “an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” “I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company,” Huang wrote in his statement. He has also been called on by Congress to provide a closed-door briefing on his interactions with Alice Huang, the Times reported. As the artificial intelligence industry surge has spurred Nvidia’s stock prices to new heights, Huang has appeared at US President Donald Trump’s side at White House events, as recently as last month when he accepted a National Medal of Science from the Republican leader. Huang was among the world’s most influential tech leaders — including Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos and Mark Zuckerberg — who vowed to self-regulate AI against possible threats, as Trump rejected calls for government oversight and dismissed warnings the technology could wipe out humanity. Nvidia shareholders filed a class action lawsuit against Huang and the AI chip maker for failing to disclose information about the relationship to investors. Nvidia shares have plummeted in recent days since Huang admitted to the affair. item.title: Data sovereignty takes more than keeping data close to home
item.description: Keeping sensitive data within national borders might satisfy a residency requirement. But does it mean your organization is genuinely in control? Not necessarily. Data could be stored locally while remaining subject to another jurisdiction's laws, dependent on overseas service providers or exposed to disruption beyond your control. For enterprise IT teams, that distinction is becoming harder to ignore. Geopolitical tensions, evolving regulations and the growing use of AI are forcing organizations to reconsider what data sovereignty means in practice. Yet translating those concerns into a workable strategy is another matter. And simply throwing more money at the problem won't necessarily solve it. In The Register's on-demand webinar, Data Sovereignty By Design, moderator Tim Phillips speaks with Patrick Smith, Field CTO for EMEA at Everpure, formerly Pure Storage, about moving beyond compliance checklists and taking a more strategic approach to data control. Drawing on findings from Everpure's research, Smith explores a curious disconnect: organizations are increasing their investment in sovereignty initiatives, yet many still lack a coordinated strategy. Some of the risks attracting the most attention aren't necessarily those receiving the greatest investment. The discussion examines why sovereignty shouldn't be treated as an IT-only responsibility. Decisions about which data needs protection, which services must remain operational and what level of risk is acceptable require input from business leaders, security, procurement and legal teams. There's also the question of priorities. Not every workload needs the same sovereign controls, and attempting to protect everything equally can make an already complicated challenge considerably harder. Smith explains the concept of the "minimum viable company," identifying the critical services, applications and data an organization needs to keep operating through disruption. He also considers why visibility into data access, supplier dependencies and potential exit strategies should influence technology decisions from the outset. For IT leaders trying to turn sovereignty from an abstract boardroom concern into something actionable, the conversation offers useful questions to take back to their organizations. Because knowing where your data sits is one thing. Knowing whether you can maintain control when circumstances change is quite another. item.title: Your AI agent is only as good as your endpoint data
item.description: Every so often a flaw comes along that shows how fast the ground can shift under IT and security teams. PHP2Shell, a pair of critical flaws in PHP, was one of them. Details leaked before the planned disclosure, frontier AI helped researchers find the flaws, and PHP shipped fixes the next day. For many teams, though, the patch was the easy part. So what does it take to respond at that speed, and where should teams begin? What does governed autonomous IT look like in practice? Picture a loop. Software finds where a risk lives and ranks what matters most. It proposes a fix, then, inside limits people define, carries it out and checks that it worked. Routine, low-risk actions can run on their own. Higher-impact ones wait for a person to approve. A few are never handed over at all. Each step leaves a record that someone can review and reverse. What challenges do IT and security teams face today? Three problems keep coming up. The first is visibility. PHP2Shell reportedly sat undetected for more than a decade. For these two flaws, the fix was a version upgrade. The hard part was finding every copy of PHP, including copies bundled inside other software or extracted by hand onto Windows machines that never registered as installed applications. Then teams had to work out which copies the internet could reach and check for signs of earlier attack. An inventory built from a periodic snapshot can't answer those questions on the day they matter. The second is tool-hopping. Answering "where does this run, and can the internet reach it?" often means pivoting across an asset inventory, a vulnerability scanner and an external attack surface tool, each with its own view. Every hop adds delay. Every console is another chance to disagree with the last. The third is pace. Several security firms reported exploitation attempts before PHP released its fixes, and Cloudflare reported early attacks hours ahead of the patch. Frontier AI models helped find PHP2Shell, and in April Anthropic said its Claude Mythos Preview model had found thousands of previously unknown flaws across every major operating system and browser. With models like these in the picture, the old rhythm of disclose, patch and verify assumes a gap that keeps shrinking. Put an AI agent on top of stale, fragmented data and these problems don't go away. They scale. Why does real-time endpoint data make autonomy trustworthy? Endpoints are where work happens and where many attacks end up, so they are the ground truth for any decision about the estate. Four qualities make that data a sound foundation for autonomous action: Accuracy: Live data from the endpoints themselves, not a snapshot that was true last week. Speed: A short path from question to action, with no hopping between tools to reconcile answers. Control: Approvals and an audit trail, plus the ability to roll back, so any automated action can be reviewed and reversed. item.title: COP31: UK Makes History, Appoints World’s First ‘Climate Security’ Envoy
item.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced on Thursday the appointment of a special envoy focused on “climate security”, a world first, to better prepare for the growing impacts of global warming. In a speech to the UN’s COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, the Labour leader recalled that he spent his first three weeks as prime minister this past summer responding to the worst wildfires Britain ever experienced. “I decided then it was important for me to be here to show British leadership in a world where climate issues have taken too much of a backseat,” said Burnham, who was the only G7 leader attending the summit. UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres delivers a speech during the High-Level Segment for Heads of States and Government at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) at the Antalya Expo Center in Antalya on November 11, 2026. Britain and the rest of western Europe experienced their hottest summer on record, with a succession of heatwaves and wildfires. The heat caused tens of thousands of excess deaths on the continent. “Climate is a national security issue,” Burnham said. “As evidence of that, I am today announcing the appointment of Dame Madeleine Alessandri as the first UK special representative for climate security,” he said. Swedish activist Greta Thunberg arrives at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, on November 10, 2026. Alessandri is the former head of the UK’s Joint Intelligence Committee, the body that briefs ministers on security threats. “In this role, I will work with partners across government and internationally to strengthen our understanding of climate threats, build resilience, and ensure we are better prepared for the challenges ahead,” Alessandri said in a statement. Brazil’s President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva delivers a speech during the High-Level Segment for Heads of States and Government at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) at the Antalya Expo Center in Antalya on November 11, 2026. Photo by OZAN KOSE / AFP Britain has a climate minister, Katie White, who is in Antalya for the COP31 talks that are scheduled to end on November 20. Cosima Cassel, an expert at climate think-tank E3G, said countries often have climate envoys and climate security is part of their remit. “This is the first climate security envoy specifically,” she told AFP. “This appointment elevates that issue to the level it deserves, and other governments should consider a similar model,” Cassel said. This handout photograph taken and released by Turkish Presidency Press Office on November 10, 2026, shows Turkey’s President Recep Tayyip Erdogan (C,R) meeting with UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres (C,L) during the COP31 UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya. Environmental group Greenpeace also said the appointment was a “welcome move” as climate change is a “threat multiplier”. item.title: Court orders extradition of Nigerian to US over alleged wire fraud, others
item.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja has ordered the extradition of a Nigerian, Temitope Omotade, to the U.S. District Court of Minnesota to face his trial over allegations bordering on wire fraud, among others. Justice Peter Lifu, in a judgment, held that the application made by the Attorney-General of the Federation (AGF) was meritorious. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the AGF had made the application for the extradition of Omotade to the U.S. He is a suspect in a superseding five-count indictment bordering on five counts in case number 22-CR-24 SRN/HB filed on Feb. 8, 2022, at the US District Court. The offences in counts one, two and three bordered on mail and wire fraud in violation of Title 18 US Code, Sections 1341 and 1343, and 1349, which carries a maximum penalty of 30 years in prison in each of the counts. Counts four and five bordered on aggravated identity theft and aiding and abetting, in violation of Title 18 US Codes, Sections 1028A (a)(1) and 2, which carries a maximum penalty of two years in prison for each count, consecutive to any other term of imprisonment imposed on the defendant. In the AGF’s application, he contended that the request was grounded on an extradition packet and diplomatic notes from the US, including a sealed indictment from the U.S. District Court for the District of Minnesota and a warrant for Omotade’s arrest. He argued that all statutory requirements under the Extradition Act have been met because the offences are non-political, non-trivial, and made in good faith. He submitted that the Central Authority Unit had established that proper certifications and documentation, including affidavits from US officials, relevant statute copies, and passport details, accompanied the formal request. Besides, the AGF said there were no pending local criminal proceedings in Nigeria against Omotade for the specified offences, and adequate assurances regarding nonprejudicial trial conditions in the US had been secured. He asserted that the request and accompanying materials satisfied all conditions for the surrender of Omotade, who was the sole respondent in the suit marked FHC/ABJ/CS/494/2024. The AGF maintained that the legal procedures complied with the Oaths Act and the Extradition Act, adding that the interest of justice dictated that the request be granted, “as the respondent is duly accused of the indictments brought against him abroad.” But Omotade, in his counter-affidavit filed by his lawyer, prayed the court to dismiss the suit. Omotade denied all allegations of mail fraud, wire fraud, conspiracy, and aggravated identity theft, maintaining that his connection to Roxanne Gilbert involved no criminal conduct or digital proceeds. He contended that the extradition application lacked substantive proof and statutory backing for several reasons. According to him, the supporting documents lack any blockchain analysis, financial trails, chat histories, or video calls, reducing the case to mere identification p

item.title: Oil: Nigeria cautions Namibia against host community neglect
item.description: By Folarin Kehinde Nigeria has urged Namibia to establish clear policies on host community benefits, local content development and environmental protection before commencing commercial oil production, warning the emerging oil-producing country against repeating the challenges that have characterised Nigeria’s petroleum industry. Nigeria’s High Commissioner to Namibia, Ambassador Esther Adebola Arewa, gave the advice while delivering the keynote address titled: Nigeria-Namibia at the 5th International African Energy, Oil and Gas Summit in Windhoek, Namibia. Arewa said Namibia could draw important lessons from Nigeria’s nearly seven decades of oil exploration, particularly its experiences with gas flaring, community grievances, regulatory uncertainty and inadequate local participation. She urged the Namibian government to make adequate provisions for communities in oil-producing areas before the first barrel of crude oil is produced. “Decide now, before the first barrel, how the people of ǁKaras and the coastal towns will share in this, and write it down,” she said. The envoy stressed that establishing trust with host communities before production begins would help prevent conflicts and costly disputes in the future. “It is far cheaper to build trust before production than to buy back peace afterwards,” she added. Her warning comes as Namibia advances petroleum exploration in the Orange Basin, which has attracted significant international interest. Arewa identified gas utilisation, regulatory certainty, local content development and host community participation as four major lessons Namibia should draw from Nigeria’s experience. On gas utilisation, she said Nigeria had wasted substantial quantities of associated gas through flaring for decades but had made progress in reducing the practice. She disclosed that nearly 93 per cent of the gas produced in Nigeria in the first half of 2026 was put to use, while the country’s gas reserves stood at about 215 trillion cubic feet. She said Nigeria was willing to share its technical expertise with Namibia, particularly in managing associated gas from offshore petroleum operations. On regulatory reforms, Arewa recalled that Nigeria spent more than a decade debating comprehensive petroleum legislation before the Petroleum Industry Act was enacted in August 2021. According to her, the prolonged uncertainty affected investor confidence and drove some investors away. “Investors waited. Some of them left. Certainty, even imperfect certainty, is worth a great deal,” she said. The High Commissioner also cited Nigeria’s local content policy as an example of how deliberate government intervention could increase domestic participation in the oil and gas industry. She said Nigerian content in the petroleum sector rose from about 26 per cent in 2016 to 61 per cent in 2026, with a target of 70 per cent. item.title: FG urged to engage Oyedepo, Ibiyeomie, Enenche, Komaiya on development
item.description: The Federal Government has been urged to engage prominent Nigerian Christian leaders, including Bishop David Oyedepo, Pastor David Ibiyeomie, Dr Paul Enenche and Pastor Korede Komaiya, to explore how their religious institutions could contribute to addressing the country’s development challenges. The Convener of the Christian Youth Forum, James Paul Adama, made the call in an article titled, “Why the Nigerian Government Must Invite Bishop David Oyedepo and His Spiritual Sons Immediately.” Adama argued that the institutions established by the clerics had developed structures and community-based initiatives that could provide useful lessons for national development. He said their contributions to education, healthcare, transportation, employment generation, infrastructure and poverty reduction demonstrated how faith-based organisations could complement government efforts. The article highlighted the free transportation services operated by some of the churches to convey worshippers to services and other programmes, describing the arrangements as examples of organised social support. Adama also drew attention to investments by the religious organisations in primary and secondary education, as well as universities equipped with modern learning facilities. He said the institutions combined academic development with character building to prepare young Nigerians for leadership and responsible citizenship. On healthcare, he cited medical outreaches, financial assistance to patients, sponsorship of surgeries and support for Nigerians seeking specialised medical treatment abroad. He added that scholarship programmes operated by the churches had helped young people from disadvantaged backgrounds gain access to education and professional qualifications. item.title: Trump to flex muscles on Asia tour after midterms losses
item.description: After his party suffered a midterms hammering, President Donald Trump faces a new challenge: proving he is still the boss of US foreign policy on the global stage. With Trump politically hamstrung as he enters the remaining two-year ‘lame duck’ period of his White House tenure, world leaders may be quietly wondering how to leverage the new balance of power in Washington. The 80-year-old Republican heads to the ASEAN summit in the Philippines and APEC summit in China from a radically transformed and hostile political landscape at home after the Democrats seized both the House of Representatives and Senate. Constitutionally banned from seeking a third term in the 2028 presidential race, the unpredictable billionaire could be all the more inclined to focus his energy on the international stage. “After bad midterms, this is how presidents reset,” Edgard Kagan, an expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) told a news briefing. – Iran, trade, China – That is especially true for Trump on his Asian tour, where he is unlikely to be pressed publicly on domestic politics. China has described the midterms as an “internal affair” and said it is “willing to continue working” with the United States after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress. But the power shift in Washington will still be on leaders’ radars, said Joshua Kurlantzick, an expert in Southeast Asia and South Asia at the Council on Foreign Relations. “In private, many (Asian) leaders are relieved,” Kurlantzick wrote in an article this month. “The Iran war has been particularly challenging for the United States’ Asian partners and allies, and they hope that after the midterm results US President Donald Trump’s decision-making on the issue will become more predictable.” Trump has said several times since the midterms that renewed fighting between the United States and Iran is unlikely. A Democratic-controlled Congress could also take a tougher stance towards China, Kurlantzick added, backtracking on the Trump administration’s “soft approach” to Beijing that has sparked unease among US allies in Asia. Leaders in the world’s largest continent are also hoping to see Democrats push back on Trump’s barrage of tariffs on trading partners, which have stung Asian economies heavily reliant on exports. Democratic House leader Hakeem Jeffries has urged Congress to reassert its authority over US trade policy. The Democrats will not get an easy ride in undoing Trump’s policies, though. The president enjoys broad authority over trade and holds veto power over congressional legislation — which he has vowed to use. – High-profile meeting – Trump relishes dramatic gestures and foreign policy provides an ideal arena for high-profile meetings, such as with Chinese and Russian leaders Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. item.title: Clint Eastwood's Legendary Western Sequel Is Waiting to Be Discovered on Streaming
item.description: In 1964, Italian director Sergio Leone redefined the Western movie genre with A Fistful of Dollars . Eschewing the relatively simplistic morality tales of earlier films, Leone’s protagonist wasn’t a noble hero, but an opportunistic gunslinger who pits two rival Old West gangs against each other to score a big payday. Despite the moral complexity of it all — or, more likely, because of it — A Fistful of Dollars was an international success that proved three things: audiences were ready for a new kind of Western, America no longer had a monopoly on the genre, and Clint Eastwood was a bankable movie star.

item.title: Who could potentially replace Jensen Huang if Nvidia ousts him?
item.description: Chip giant Nvidia’s board was reportedly meeting Wednesday to discuss the future of co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang after he dated an accused Chinese spy, according to US media. The 63-year-old tech titan, who has led the key AI giant since it was founded in 1993, has been beleaguered with reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang, a data center executive who has been accused by US intelligence of working for China’s Ministry of State Security. With Huang unexpectedly on the backfoot, and no known plan of succession at Nvidia, the field is wide open for a variety of replacements to lead one of the key AI players should the board decide to oust Huang. Here are some of the names being suggested most frequently as Huang’s potential successor. Internal hire With over 40,000 employees, Nvidia could opt to go with an in-house pick to take the helm, including one of Huang’s dozens of direct reports. Tech publications frequently cited Nvidia’s Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as an easy choice, if for no other reason than she is already among top leadership at the chip behemoth. Another longtime Nvidia honcho is Ian Buck, who oversees the company’s data center clients. He was a key mind behind the software that keeps Nvidia-designed chips in demand. Business magazine Inc. also lists Nvidia’s vice president of applied deep learning research, Bryan Catanzaro, as a possible pick. A family affair Huang could also try and position a member of his own family as his replacement, with more than one option for a bloodline succession. His daughter Madison Huang is currently the senior director of product marketing at Nvidia and is among the names most suggested by analysts. As a marketing leader, she had a multi-year stint at luxury conglomerate LVMH. Jensen Huang’s son Spencer Huang could also be a potential successor. He currently works at Nvidia as the director of product management in the company’s robotics division. Huang’s cousin, Lisa Su, could also be a viable candidate for selection – not only is she his first cousin, once removed, but she also has valuable expertise as the longtime CEO of semiconductor giant AMD. Tech CEO swap Su is not the only tech chief being bandied around as a possible replacement for Huang. Rene Haas, CEO of UK chip design firm Arm, is another candidate being suggested by the tech press. Speculation runs wide in Silicon Valley, where former Apple CEO Tim Cook – who stepped down from leading the tech giant in August after 15 years at the helm – is another person insiders say could potentially be tapped.
